symbols.name: Gate valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two open triangles meeting tip to tip on the pipe (a bow-tie), with nothing in the middle. A handwheel stem (a T on top) is optional.
symbols.meaning: Manual isolation valve, normally fully open or fully closed, not for throttling. On PIP/ISA-style legends the plain bow-tie is the gate valve; on ISO 10628 drawings the plain bow-tie is a generic valve, so check the legend.
variants: ISO 10628-2: the plain bow-tie means "valve, general"
Filled (black) bow-tie: normally closed
Some legends add a short vertical bar at the tips to mean gate specifically
Size/class appear only in the line number, not in the symbol

symbols.name: Globe valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with a solid black dot where the triangle tips meet.
symbols.meaning: Manual throttling valve: regulating flow, control-valve bypasses, and vents and drains that are opened slowly. A globe body with an actuator on top is a control valve (see act-diaphragm).
variants: Some legends draw the dot as a small filled circle with a stem and handwheel
Bypass globe valves around a control valve are normally closed: the body or dot may be filled
Look-alikes: open circle = ball valve, small rectangle = plug valve

symbols.name: Ball valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with an open (white) circle at the centre, where the tips meet.
symbols.meaning: Quarter-turn isolation valve: full-bore isolation, pigging lines, ESD and on/off duty when actuated. Small sizes have a lever, large ones a gear.
variants: Full-bore vs reduced-bore is usually written as FB / RB next to the symbol
Trunnion vs floating is not shown, only on the valve datasheet
Look-alikes: filled dot = globe valve, small rectangle = plug valve

symbols.name: Butterfly valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two short vertical lines across the pipe (wafer body between flanges) with a diagonal line through the middle (the disc) and a dot at its centre (the shaft).
symbols.meaning: Quarter-turn disc valve used for large low-pressure lines: seawater, cooling water, firewater and HVAC. Can isolate or throttle.
variants: Very common alternative (PIP-style): a bow-tie with a vertical line through the centre and a dot
Some legends draw the disc as a thin ellipse instead of a line
Triple-offset (metal-seated) types are only identified on the datasheet

symbols.name: Plug valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with a small upright rectangle (the plug) at the centre.
symbols.meaning: Quarter-turn valve with a tapered or cylindrical plug, often lubricated. Used for isolation in sandy or dirty service and on wellhead / manifold duties.
variants: Some legends fill the rectangle
Multi-port plug valves are drawn with three or four triangles (see the 3-way valve)
Look-alikes: open circle = ball valve, filled dot = globe valve

symbols.name: Needle valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Small bow-tie with a stem carrying a solid triangle pointing down onto the body (the needle), topped by a handwheel bar.
symbols.meaning: Fine-throttling instrument valve, ½" and below: instrument roots, gauge isolation, sample and purge lines. Usually not modelled at plant scale.
variants: Often drawn without the needle as a plain small bow-tie on an instrument impulse line
Instrument manifolds (2-, 3-, 5-valve) are drawn as boxes or groups of small valves

symbols.name: Diaphragm valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with a curved arc (the diaphragm bonnet) spanning the top of the body where the tips meet, and a stem above.
symbols.meaning: Valve that closes by pressing an elastomer diaphragm onto a weir. Used for corrosive, slurry or chemical-injection service. No dedicated 3D component; use globe-valve and note the real type.
variants: Some legends draw a small dome or a horizontal bar above the tips
Weir type vs straight-through is only on the datasheet

symbols.name: Pinch valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A flexible sleeve: two curved lines bowing in towards the centre between short end bars, with two solid arrowheads pressing in from above and below.
symbols.meaning: Valve that closes by squeezing a rubber sleeve. Used for slurry, sand and abrasive service. Rare offshore. No dedicated component; use a generic valve and note it.
variants: Legends vary widely: some show a bow-tie with "P" or "PINCH" beside it
Air-operated pinch valves show the air connection to the body

symbols.name: Knife gate valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with a thin upright rectangle (the knife blade) through the centre that rises above the body, then a stem and handwheel bar.
symbols.meaning: Gate valve with a sharpened blade that cuts through solids. Used for slurry, sand, drains and low-pressure bulk lines.
variants: Some legends draw only a vertical line through the tips
Look-alike: needle valve has a solid triangle on the stem, not a blade

symbols.name: Angle valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two triangles at right angles: one pointing in from the side (inlet) and one pointing up from below (outlet), tips meeting, with a stem and handwheel on top.
symbols.meaning: Globe-type valve whose outlet is at 90° to the inlet. Common for drains, chokes and blowdown. A spring on top makes it a relief valve, not an angle valve.
variants: A dot at the tips makes it an angle globe valve
With an actuator it is an angle control valve
With a spring or a pilot box it is a PSV (see relief)

symbols.name: Three-way valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Three triangles meeting tip to tip: left, right and one pointing up from below, each with a pipe stub. Usually carries an actuator or handwheel.
symbols.meaning: Diverting or mixing valve, e.g. a cooling-medium bypass (TCV) or a PSV changeover. With an actuator, arrows on the ports show the failed flow path. No dedicated component; use ball-valve or control-valve and note it.
variants: A filled triangle marks the port that is normally closed
PSV changeover (interlocked) valves are often drawn as a pair of 3-way valves joined by a dashed mechanical link
Plug-type 3-way bodies show a small rectangle at the centre

symbols.name: Four-way valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Four triangles meeting at one point, like two bow-ties crossed, with a pipe stub on every side.
symbols.meaning: Four-port diverter: flow reversal (e.g. backflushing a filter or a meter prover diverter). No dedicated component.
variants: Filled triangles mark closed ports
Prover four-way diverters are often drawn as a box labelled "4-way"

symbols.name: Normally closed valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with both triangles filled solid black.
symbols.meaning: The valve is closed in normal operation: drains, bypasses, crossovers, spare connections. Read the body type from the legend; the fill only means closed. Set the valve normally closed in the model.
variants: Some legends fill only the inner part, or write NC beside an open bow-tie
Filled globe, ball or plug valves keep their centre mark
A few old legends use filled bodies for check valves instead, so check the legend

symbols.name: Locked open valve
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A valve body with the letters "LO" written beside or above it.
symbols.meaning: The valve is locked in the open position, for example the isolation valves under a PSV or on a vent, so it cannot be shut by mistake. Model it as normally open and note "LO". The lock or seal is a padlock or chain; the body type is read from the bow-tie, and gate-valve is only the default.
variants: The letters can be below the body or at the end of a leader
Some legends add a small padlock or a "C" hook
Ball valves with LO/LC have an open circle in the bow-tie

symbols.name: Locked closed valve
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A valve body with the letters "LC" written beside or above it. The body is often drawn filled because the valve is closed.
symbols.meaning: The valve is locked closed, for example a drain or a spool to a flare, so it cannot be opened by mistake. Model it as normally closed and note "LC". The lock or seal is a padlock or chain; the body type is read from the bow-tie, and gate-valve is only the default.
variants: The letters can be below the body or at the end of a leader
Some legends add a small padlock or a "C" hook
Ball valves with LO/LC have an open circle in the bow-tie

symbols.name: Car-sealed open valve
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A valve body with the letters "CSO" written beside or above it.
symbols.meaning: The valve is sealed open with a car seal. Breaking the seal needs a permit, and seals are audited. Typical on PSV inlet and outlet isolations. Model it as normally open and note "CSO". The lock or seal is a numbered car seal (wire tag); the body type is read from the bow-tie, and gate-valve is only the default.
variants: The letters can be below the body or at the end of a leader
Some legends add a small padlock or a "C" hook
Ball valves with LO/LC have an open circle in the bow-tie

symbols.name: Car-sealed closed valve
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A valve body with the letters "CSC" written beside or above it. The body is often drawn filled because the valve is closed.
symbols.meaning: The valve is sealed closed with a car seal. Model it as normally closed and note "CSC". The lock or seal is a numbered car seal (wire tag); the body type is read from the bow-tie, and gate-valve is only the default.
variants: The letters can be below the body or at the end of a leader
Some legends add a small padlock or a "C" hook
Ball valves with LO/LC have an open circle in the bow-tie

symbols.name: Float-operated valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 21, valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with a stem rising to a horizontal lever that ends in a circle (the float).
symbols.meaning: Self-acting level valve (ball-cock): tank make-up water, diesel day tank fill, drain pots. No instrument loop; the float moves the valve directly.
variants: Sometimes drawn with a dashed mechanical link from the valve to a float inside the tank
Tagged LCV (self-actuated level control valve)

symbols.name: Double block and bleed
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / API 6D (DBB / DIB)
symbols.drawn: Two isolation valves in series on the pipe with a small bleed valve on a branch between them, often inside a dashed box when it is a single-body DBB valve.
symbols.meaning: Positive isolation for maintenance: both blocks are shut and the cavity between them is bled to a safe place. Required on high-pressure hydrocarbon isolations and instrument connections. Model the block valves as ball-valve or gate-valve and list the bleed as not modelled.
variants: Single-body DBB valves (two balls in one body) are drawn as one box with two bow-ties
The bleed may go to a closed drain or a vent line
Instrument DBB manifolds are often shown as a single rectangle labelled DBB

symbols.name: Damper (louvre)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 / HVAC practice (ISO 14617-8)
symbols.drawn: A rectangle across the duct with several parallel slanted blades inside.
symbols.meaning: Duct damper on HVAC, fired-heater stack or fan systems. A fire damper (FD) closes on fire; a gas-tight damper isolates enclosures on gas detection. No dedicated component.
variants: Single-blade dampers look like a butterfly valve on a duct
Fire dampers may be marked FD or carry a fusible-link note
Motorised dampers carry an M actuator

symbols.name: Fixed (positive) choke
symbols.standard: API 6A / company wellhead legend
symbols.drawn: An angle body (inlet triangle from the side, outlet triangle below) with a plain cap on top instead of a handwheel, and an orifice (a split bar) across the outlet.
symbols.meaning: Wellhead or manifold choke with a fixed-size bean (orifice). Changing rate means changing the bean, so there is no handwheel. Sits on the christmas-tree wing outlet.
variants: Some legends draw a bow-tie with "CH" or a bean (small black rectangle) inside
Bean size is written as a fraction of an inch in 64ths, e.g. 32/64"

symbols.name: Adjustable choke
symbols.standard: API 6A / ISO 14617 (adjustability arrow)
symbols.drawn: An angle body with a handwheel stem and a long diagonal arrow through the body (the ISO mark for "adjustable").
symbols.meaning: Wellhead choke whose opening is set by hand or by an actuator (with an actuator it is a choke control valve, often HCV or PCV). Controls well rate and drops pressure from wellhead to manifold.
variants: Actuated chokes carry a stepping actuator or an M motor
Some legends draw a bow-tie with a diagonal arrow
Choke position may be shown as % or 64ths

symbols.name: Check valve (general)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 22, check valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with the downstream (outlet) triangle filled black, and a flow arrow above it.
symbols.meaning: Non-return valve: flow only in the arrow direction. Found on pump discharges, compressor discharges and anywhere back-flow must be stopped. The filled side points the way flow goes. Swing type is the default when the legend does not say.
variants: ISA/US style: an open triangle against a vertical bar (the seat), with or without an arrow
Some legends draw "N" or "NRV" beside a plain bow-tie
Check the arrow, not the fill, for direction if the drawing is mirrored

symbols.name: Swing check valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 22, check valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two vertical end bars across the pipe with a disc hanging diagonally from a pivot dot at the top (the hinged clapper), and a flow arrow above.
symbols.meaning: Check valve with a hinged disc that swings open with flow. The usual type for horizontal liquid lines and large pipe.
variants: Often drawn simply as the general check (bow-tie with one side filled)
Tilting-disc check valves are drawn the same way

symbols.name: Lift (piston) check valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 22, check valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Bow-tie with the outlet triangle filled and an open circle (the piston or disc) where the tips meet, with a flow arrow above.
symbols.meaning: Globe-pattern check valve with a piston or disc that lifts off its seat. Good for high pressure, small bore and pulsating flow (reciprocating pumps and compressors).
variants: Some legends draw a globe-valve body with an arrow
Look-alike: ball check (ball in front of a seat bar), stop-check (adds a handwheel)

symbols.name: Ball check valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 22, check valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An open triangle pointing downstream at a small black ball, which sits against a vertical bar (the seat).
symbols.meaning: Check valve with a free ball. Used on small lines, metering-pump discharges and chemical injection. No dedicated component; use check-valve-piston if it must be modelled.
variants: Some legends draw a bow-tie with a filled circle in the outlet side
Injection check valves at the quill are often drawn as this symbol

symbols.name: Dual-plate check valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 22, check valves) / PIP PIC001 / API 594
symbols.drawn: Two vertical bars (a wafer between flanges) with two short plates hinged at the centre and opening downstream in a "<" shape, and a flow arrow above.
symbols.meaning: Wafer check valve with two spring-loaded half-discs on a central hinge pin. Short and light, so common on compressor and pump discharges and on large water lines.
variants: Many legends just use the general check symbol and write "dual plate" or "DPC"
Some draw a single vertical bar with a filled triangle

symbols.name: Stop-check valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 22, check valves) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A lift check (bow-tie, outlet filled, open circle at the centre) with a stem and handwheel on top, and a flow arrow beside it.
symbols.meaning: Screw-down non-return valve: acts as a check valve, but the handwheel can also hold it shut. Used on boiler feeds and parallel pump discharges. No dedicated component; use check-valve-piston and note the handwheel.
variants: Some legends draw a globe valve with an arrow and a handwheel

symbols.name: Pressure safety valve (spring loaded)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 23, safety valves and fittings) / PIP PIC001 / API 520 / ISA 5.1
symbols.drawn: An angle body with the inlet from below and the outlet to the side, and a zig-zag spring on top capped by a short bar. A PSV bubble with the loop number usually sits beside it (not drawn here), with the set pressure and the orifice size (e.g. "3L4").
symbols.meaning: Last-line overpressure protection. It lifts at the set pressure and relieves to flare, vent or atmosphere. Inlet size, orifice letter and outlet size read "3L4" = 3" inlet, L orifice, 4" outlet. TSVs are small thermal-relief valves on blocked-in liquid lines.
variants: Bellows-balanced PSVs have a small bellows drawn under the spring
Some legends draw a straight-through body with a spring
PSVs often sit between LO/CSO isolation valves, with a spare PSV on a changeover valve

symbols.name: Pilot-operated relief valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 23, safety valves and fittings) / PIP PIC001 / API 520
symbols.drawn: An angle relief body with a piston chamber (a box) on top instead of a spring, and a small spring-loaded pilot beside it with a sensing line back to the inlet.
symbols.meaning: Relief valve whose main piston is held shut by inlet pressure and released by a small pilot. Tight up to the set point, so used where operating pressure is close to set pressure (gas export, large flare loads).
variants: The pilot can be drawn as a small PSV symbol or a box with "P"
Remote-sensing pilots have the sensing line run to the vessel, not the valve inlet

symbols.name: Pressure-vacuum (breather) valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 23, safety valves and fittings) / PIP PIC001 / API 520 / API 2000
symbols.drawn: A housing on a tank nozzle with two arrows inside: one pointing up (pressure relief out) and one pointing down (vacuum relief in), each over a weighted pallet.
symbols.meaning: Tank breather valve on atmospheric tanks (API 650/2000). It vents vapour when the tank fills or heats and lets air in when it empties. No dedicated component; note it on the storage-tank.
variants: Vacuum breakers alone show only the down arrow
Often combined with a flame arrester below it
Some legends draw a PSV symbol with "P/V" beside it

symbols.name: Rupture disc (bursting disc)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 23, safety valves and fittings) / PIP PIC001 / API 520 / ISO 4126-2
symbols.drawn: Two short parallel bars (the holder) across a vertical pipe, with a curved arc between them bulging towards the outlet.
symbols.meaning: Non-reclosing relief device that bursts at a set pressure. Used alone, or under a PSV to protect it from corrosion (then a pressure gauge or PI is drawn between them). ISA tag is PSE. Becomes rupture-disc.
variants: Some legends draw a vertical pipe with a dashed or zig-zag line across it
Buckling-pin relief valves are drawn as a body with a pin and tagged PSE too

symbols.name: Flame arrester
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 23, safety valves and fittings) / PIP PIC001 / API 520 / ISO 16852
symbols.drawn: An in-line rectangle on the pipe with zig-zag lines inside (the crimped-metal element).
symbols.meaning: Passive device that stops a flame front passing down a vent line or into a tank. Found on tank vents, drain-tank vents and on vent stacks. No dedicated component.
variants: Detonation arresters are drawn the same and marked "DA"
Some legends use a rectangle with crossed diagonal hatching

symbols.name: Self-actuated pressure regulator (PCV)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009 (self-actuated regulators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A bow-tie body with a diaphragm dome on its stem, a spring above the dome, and a thin sensing line from the dome to the pipe downstream of the valve.
symbols.meaning: Pressure-reducing regulator with no instrument loop: downstream pressure acts on the diaphragm directly. Fuel gas, instrument air, nitrogen and blanket gas. Tag PCV. No dedicated component; control-valve is the closest stand-in.
variants: Internal sensing: no external line is drawn
Some legends draw the sensing line as a dashed or plain thin line
Blanketing regulators sit on a tank roof

symbols.name: Back-pressure regulator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009 (self-actuated regulators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Like the pressure regulator, but the thin sensing line runs from the dome to the pipe upstream of the valve.
symbols.meaning: Holds upstream pressure: it opens as upstream pressure rises. Used on separator gas outlets to flare, pump minimum-flow and seal systems. No dedicated component.
variants: Some legends write "BPR" beside it
Look at which side the sensing line goes to; that is the controlled side

symbols.name: Self-actuated temperature regulator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009 (self-actuated regulators, filled-system capillary)
symbols.drawn: A bow-tie body with a diaphragm dome, and a capillary (line with small × marks) running from the dome to a sensing bulb.
symbols.meaning: Thermostatic valve driven by a filled bulb: lube-oil coolers, tracing and jacket water. No instrument loop and no dedicated component.
variants: The bulb may be drawn as a thermowell in the process line
Wax-element 3-way thermostatic valves are drawn as a 3-way valve with TCV

symbols.name: Excess-flow valve
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A bow-tie with a spring drawn inside the inlet triangle and a flow arrow above.
symbols.meaning: Closes automatically when flow exceeds a set rate (a line break downstream). Found on instrument connections, LPG and chemical lines. No dedicated component.
variants: Usually just a check-valve-like symbol tagged EFV
Some legends write "XS" or "EFV" next to a plain bow-tie

symbols.name: Handwheel operator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A valve body with a stem and a short horizontal bar on top (the handwheel), a "T".
symbols.meaning: Manual valve operated by a handwheel. The body below tells the valve type; the handwheel just confirms it is manual. Tag HV if it has one.
variants: Most legends omit the handwheel on manual valves altogether
Hand-operated control valves are tagged HCV

symbols.name: Lever operator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A ball-valve body with a short stem and a lever drawn as a slanted line from the top of the stem.
symbols.meaning: Quarter-turn valve with a lever handle: small ball, plug and butterfly valves (typically 4" and below).
variants: Some legends draw the lever horizontally
A padlock or "LO" beside the lever means locked open

symbols.name: Gear operator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A valve body with a small square box (gearbox) on its stem, and a handwheel shaft coming out of the side of the box.
symbols.meaning: Manual valve with a gearbox, for large or high-pressure quarter-turn valves (ball, plug, butterfly) where a lever would be too hard to move.
variants: Some legends draw a handwheel T with "G" or "GO" beside it
Bevel-gear operators on gate valves are drawn the same

symbols.name: Manual operator with position indicator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001 (local indication)
symbols.drawn: A handwheel valve with a small half-round dial with a pointer beside the stem, or a ZI bubble linked to the stem.
symbols.meaning: Manual valve with a local open/closed position indicator, often required on firewater and deluge isolation valves so the position can be checked at a glance.
variants: ISA style: a ZI bubble joined to the stem by a short line
Rising-stem gate valves are sometimes noted "OS&Y" (outside screw and yoke) instead

symbols.name: Diaphragm actuator (control valve)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A bow-tie (often with a globe dot) with a stem and a dome-shaped head on top (a half circle sitting on a flat bar).
symbols.meaning: Pneumatic spring-diaphragm actuator: the classic modulating control valve. Its tag (FV/LV/PV/TV) names the loop, and FO/FC beside it gives the fail position. Becomes control-valve.
variants: The dome may be drawn flat-topped or as a full ellipse
A positioner box on the stem is common
The body may be a butterfly or ball with the same dome for rotary control valves

symbols.name: Valve positioner
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A control valve with a small box on the stem below the dome (the positioner), joined to the stem, with a signal line entering the box.
symbols.meaning: Positioner on a control valve: compares the controller signal with stem position and drives the actuator. An accessory of the control valve; it is not modelled separately.
variants: Smart (HART/fieldbus) positioners may be shown as a bubble with ZC or as a box with "P"
Many P&IDs omit the positioner and show it only in the instrument index

symbols.name: Piston actuator, single acting (spring return)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A valve with a rectangle (the cylinder) on its stem; inside it a horizontal line (the piston) with a zig-zag spring above it.
symbols.meaning: Air or hydraulic cylinder with spring return. On/off shutdown valves (ESDV, SDV, XV) use it so the spring drives the valve safe on loss of air. With an ESDV/SDV/XV tag it becomes esd-valve; with BDV it becomes blowdown-valve.
variants: Spring and piston are often omitted: a plain rectangle on the stem
Scotch-yoke quarter-turn actuators are drawn the same on a ball valve
ISA 5.1-2009 draws the piston actuator as a rectangle with the stem through it

symbols.name: Piston actuator, double acting
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A rectangle (cylinder) on the valve stem with a piston line across the middle and a signal port into each end, with no spring.
symbols.meaning: Cylinder powered in both directions. It stays put on loss of air (fail last), so it is used where the valve must not move on air failure, or with an accumulator. On/off valves (XV) mostly; use esd-valve only if the tag says ESDV/SDV.
variants: Ports may be drawn as short stubs with pneumatic (//) or hydraulic (L) marks
Often noted "FL" or "fail last"

symbols.name: Electric motor actuator (MOV)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A valve with a circle containing "M" on top of its stem.
symbols.meaning: Electric motor actuator: large isolation valves, pipeline and firewater valves, and tank valves where air is not available. It fails in place (last position) on power loss.
variants: Some legends draw a square with M
An integral control unit may be shown as a small box beside the M

symbols.name: Solenoid actuator / solenoid valve (SOV)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A square box containing "S" on the stem of a small valve, or a small S box on the air supply to a larger actuator.
symbols.meaning: Solenoid. On its own small valve it is a solenoid valve; on the air line of an ESDV actuator it is the SOV that vents the actuator to trip the valve. An accessory, not modelled separately; the main valve is what becomes esd-valve or blowdown-valve.
variants: Manual-reset solenoids add "R" in the box or beside it
De-energise-to-trip vs energise-to-trip is written on the C&E, not the symbol

symbols.name: Electro-hydraulic actuator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A rectangle on the valve stem marked "EH".
symbols.meaning: Self-contained actuator with its own electric pump and hydraulic cylinder. Used for remote, large or subsea-tie-in valves where there is no air. ESD duty makes it an esd-valve in the model.
variants: Some legends draw a hydraulic cylinder with an M beside it

symbols.name: Hydraulic actuator
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A cylinder rectangle on the stem with a piston line and "H", fed by a hydraulic signal line (a line with "L" marks).
symbols.meaning: Hydraulically powered cylinder, typical on wellhead valves (SSV/USV, wing valves) supplied from the wellhead HPU through the wellhead control panel.
variants: Wellhead surface safety valves are often drawn as a gate with a hydraulic piston and spring, tagged SSV or USV
The hydraulic supply line may be drawn without marks and just labelled HPU

symbols.name: Emergency shutdown valve (ESDV)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001 / API 6D
symbols.drawn: A ball (or gate) valve with a spring-return cylinder on the stem, a small "S" box on its air supply, and "FC" written under the body.
symbols.meaning: Shutdown valve tripped by the ESD/PSD system. It fails closed: the spring shuts it when the SOV vents the air. Inlet, outlet, riser and fuel-gas isolations. Becomes esd-valve.
variants: Some companies tag it SDV or XV; riser valves are often ESDV-R…
The body may be drawn filled when normally closed
Partial-stroke test devices and limit switches (ZSO/ZSC) are often drawn beside it

symbols.name: Blowdown valve (BDV)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (final control element actuators) / PIP PIC001 / API 521
symbols.drawn: A valve body drawn filled (normally closed) with a spring-return actuator, an "S" box, and "FO" under the body. Its outlet goes to flare.
symbols.meaning: Depressuring valve. Closed in operation and opens on ESD or fire to blow inventory down to the flare (API 521: typically to 50 % or 6.9 barg within 15 min). Fails open. Becomes blowdown-valve.
variants: Usually followed by a restriction orifice (RO) to limit the flow
Tagged BDV, or XV with an FO mark

symbols.name: Fail open (FO), arrow form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 (actuator action on failure)
symbols.drawn: A control valve with an upward arrowhead drawn on the stem between body and actuator.
symbols.meaning: On loss of air, power or signal the valve goes fully open. Typical for blowdown valves, cooling-water valves and anti-surge recycle valves. It is a property of the valve (set its fail action to FO), not a separate item.
variants: The letter form writes the letters below the body instead
The bar forms for FL/FI come from secondary sources describing ISA 5.1 and are less widely used than the letters; check the legend
On 3-way valves, arrows on the ports show the failed flow path

symbols.name: Fail closed (FC), arrow form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 (actuator action on failure)
symbols.drawn: A control valve with a downward arrowhead drawn on the stem between body and actuator.
symbols.meaning: On loss of air, power or signal the valve goes fully closed. Typical for ESD valves, feed and fuel valves. It is a property of the valve (set its fail action to FC), not a separate item.
variants: The letter form writes the letters below the body instead
The bar forms for FL/FI come from secondary sources describing ISA 5.1 and are less widely used than the letters; check the legend
On 3-way valves, arrows on the ports show the failed flow path

symbols.name: Fail locked (last position) (FL), arrow form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 (actuator action on failure)
symbols.drawn: A control valve with two short horizontal bars across the stem between body and actuator.
symbols.meaning: On loss of motive power the valve stays where it was. Typical for motor-operated and double-acting valves. It is a property of the valve (set its fail action to FL), not a separate item.
variants: The letter form writes the letters below the body instead
The bar forms for FL/FI come from secondary sources describing ISA 5.1 and are less widely used than the letters; check the legend
On 3-way valves, arrows on the ports show the failed flow path

symbols.name: Fail indeterminate (FI), arrow form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 (actuator action on failure)
symbols.drawn: A control valve with one short horizontal bar across the stem between body and actuator.
symbols.meaning: The fail position is not defined: the valve may drift. Seen on double-acting actuators without a lock-up. It is a property of the valve (set its fail action to FI), not a separate item.
variants: The letter form writes the letters below the body instead
The bar forms for FL/FI come from secondary sources describing ISA 5.1 and are less widely used than the letters; check the legend
On 3-way valves, arrows on the ports show the failed flow path

symbols.name: Fail open (FO), letter form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: The letters "FO" written just below (sometimes beside) a valve body.
symbols.meaning: On loss of air, power or signal the valve goes fully open. Typical for blowdown valves, cooling-water valves and anti-surge recycle valves. Set the valve's fail action to FO.
variants: Some legends write "AO/AC" (air to open / air to close) instead. Air-to-open means fail closed
The fail position is the shelf (no-air) position, not the normal operating position

symbols.name: Fail closed (FC), letter form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: The letters "FC" written just below (sometimes beside) a valve body.
symbols.meaning: On loss of air, power or signal the valve goes fully closed. Typical for ESD valves, feed and fuel valves. Set the valve's fail action to FC.
variants: Some legends write "AO/AC" (air to open / air to close) instead. Air-to-open means fail closed
The fail position is the shelf (no-air) position, not the normal operating position

symbols.name: Fail locked (last position) (FL), letter form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: The letters "FL" written just below (sometimes beside) a valve body.
symbols.meaning: On loss of motive power the valve stays where it was. Typical for motor-operated and double-acting valves. Set the valve's fail action to FL.
variants: Also written "FLP" or "FAIL LAST"
The fail position is the shelf (no-air) position, not the normal operating position

symbols.name: Fail indeterminate (FI), letter form
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1 / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: The letters "FI" written just below (sometimes beside) a valve body.
symbols.meaning: The fail position is not defined: the valve may drift. Seen on double-acting actuators without a lock-up. Set the valve's fail action to FI.
variants: Some legends write "AO/AC" (air to open / air to close) instead. Air-to-open means fail closed
The fail position is the shelf (no-air) position, not the normal operating position

symbols.name: Valve limit switches (ZSO / ZSC)
symbols.drawn: Two small bubbles marked ZSO and ZSC on either side of an actuated valve, joined to the stem by a short line.
symbols.meaning: Open and closed position switches on an actuated valve, wired to the DCS/SIS for valve status and ESD verification. Valve accessories: keep them as notes on the valve, not as separate items.
variants: Older drawings use ZSH (open) / ZSL (closed)
Sometimes one bubble "ZS" with "O/C" beside it
Transmitters of valve position are ZT

symbols.name: I/P converter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009 (function block)
symbols.drawn: A bubble with "Y" as the second letter (e.g. FY) with a small square beside it containing "I/P". An electric (dashed) signal goes in and a pneumatic (//) signal comes out.
symbols.meaning: Converts the 4–20 mA controller output to a 0.2–1 barg air signal for the actuator. Often built into the positioner. Accessory of the control valve; not modelled separately.
variants: Function-block letters may be E/P or I/P
Behind-panel Y functions have a dashed bar in the bubble

symbols.name: Hand switch (HS)
symbols.drawn: A bubble with "HS" and a number, with an electric (dashed) signal line to the device it operates.
symbols.meaning: Push-button or selector: local start/stop for a motor, open/close for an MOV, a manual ESD push-button (often HS with a solid bar = control room). Field HS buttons are usually on a local control station (local-control-station).
variants: A solid bar in the bubble means panel/console mounted
ESD push-buttons are sometimes HZ or ESD-PB

symbols.name: Concentric reducer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A symmetric trapezoid in the line: tall at the large end and short at the small end, with both pipe centrelines in line.
symbols.meaning: Size change on vertical lines, or where the centreline must stay put. The sizes are written beside it (e.g. 8"x6"). In plant.json the assembler inserts reducers automatically when port sizes differ.
variants: Some legends use a plain triangle
Swages (small bore, threaded or socket-weld) are drawn the same

symbols.name: Eccentric reducer, flat on top (FOT)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A trapezoid with a flat top edge and a sloped bottom edge, so the two pipe centrelines are offset. Often marked "FOT".
symbols.meaning: Eccentric reducer with the flat side up. Standard on pump suctions so no vapour pocket can form. Sizes are written beside it.
variants: The flat side may be marked only by the text FOT, with a concentric-looking symbol

symbols.name: Eccentric reducer, flat on bottom (FOB)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A trapezoid with a flat bottom edge and a sloped top, centrelines offset. Often marked "FOB".
symbols.meaning: Eccentric reducer with the flat side down. Used on pipe racks to keep the bottom of pipe level, and on lines that must drain.
variants: Marked only by the text FOB on some legends

symbols.name: Spectacle blind, open (spacer in line)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.48
symbols.drawn: A figure-8 between two flange bars: the open ring sits on the pipe, and the solid (filled) blank sits off the line.
symbols.meaning: Spectacle blind in the open position: flow passes through the ring. It is turned to the closed position for positive isolation during maintenance. Becomes spectacle-blind.
variants: Some legends write "NO" (normally open) beside it
Spectacle blinds in plant isolations are often marked NO / NC

symbols.name: Spectacle blind, closed (blank in line)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.48
symbols.drawn: A figure-8 between two flange bars: the solid (filled) blank sits on the pipe, and the open ring is off the line.
symbols.meaning: Spectacle blind in the closed position: positive isolation, nothing passes. Typical on spare connections, start-up lines and vessel isolations.
variants: Some legends write "NC" beside it
A filled circle without a ring is a spade (line blank)

symbols.name: Spade (line blank)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.48
symbols.drawn: A single solid blank between two flange bars with a short handle tab sticking out, and no ring.
symbols.meaning: Removable paddle blank: positive isolation for large sizes, where a spectacle blind would be too heavy. No dedicated component; spectacle-blind is the closest.
variants: Often drawn the same as a closed spectacle blind and labelled "SPADE"

symbols.name: Spacer (ring spacer)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.48
symbols.drawn: A single open ring between two flange bars with a short handle tab, and no blank.
symbols.meaning: The ring that is fitted in place of a spade when the line is in service. No dedicated component.
variants: Usually drawn together with a spade, one of them in the line

symbols.name: Blind flange
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.5
symbols.drawn: The pipe ends at a flange bar followed by a thicker solid bar.
symbols.meaning: Bolted blind on the end of a line or a spare nozzle. Becomes blind-flange.
variants: Some legends draw two parallel bars with the outer one thicker
Look-alike: pipe cap (a small half-round at the end, welded)

symbols.name: Flanged joint
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.5
symbols.drawn: Two short parallel bars across the pipe, close together.
symbols.meaning: Bolted flange connection, usually shown only where it matters: equipment nozzles, spool breaks, spec breaks and maintenance breaks. Becomes flanged-joint.
variants: A single bar is a flange face at an equipment nozzle
Look-alike: union has a shorter third bar in the middle

symbols.name: Pipe cap
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ASME B16.9
symbols.drawn: The pipe ends in a small half-round (a "D").
symbols.meaning: Welded or threaded cap closing a pipe end: dead legs, future connections, header ends. No dedicated component.
variants: Threaded plugs are drawn as a small filled triangle or square at the end
Look-alike: blind flange (bars, not a half-round)

symbols.name: Union
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two short bars across the pipe with a shorter third bar between them.
symbols.meaning: Threaded union, used on small-bore lines (instrument air, chemical injection, tubing) to allow disconnection. No dedicated component.
variants: Legends differ: some show "||" with a small gap, others write "U"
Hammer (wing) unions on well-test and temporary lines become hammer-union; threaded small-bore unions are part of small-bore-fitting work

symbols.name: Flexible hose
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A wavy line between two short end bars.
symbols.meaning: Flexible hose or hose assembly: loading hoses, temporary connections, vibrating equipment hook-ups, and HPU or chemical hoses. Becomes flexible-hose.
variants: Some legends draw a loop or a zig-zag
Bunkering and loading hoses may carry a breakaway coupling mark

symbols.name: Expansion joint (bellows)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A zig-zag bellows drawn above and below the pipe between two flange bars.
symbols.meaning: Metallic or rubber bellows that absorbs thermal movement or vibration: exhaust ducts, seawater pump discharges and flare headers. Becomes expansion-joint.
variants: Rubber expansion joints may be drawn as a bulged section

symbols.name: Y-strainer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A leg slanting down from the pipe at about 45°, with a dashed screen line inside and a cap at its end.
symbols.meaning: Permanent in-line strainer protecting pumps, control valves and meters. Often has a DP gauge across it. Becomes y-strainer.
variants: Some legends draw a plain diagonal line with a dashed screen
A blow-off valve may be drawn on the cap

symbols.name: Basket (T-type) strainer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A rectangle hanging below the line with a cover bar on top and a dashed U (the basket) inside.
symbols.meaning: Large-capacity strainer for pump suctions and seawater systems. Duplex units have two baskets and a changeover. T-type strainers are drawn the same way. Becomes basket-strainer.
variants: Duplex: two baskets side by side with a 3-way changeover valve
Some legends draw a circle with a dashed screen

symbols.name: Temporary (cone) strainer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A dashed cone (triangle) pointing downstream inside the pipe, just downstream of a flange pair.
symbols.meaning: Start-up strainer fitted between flanges for commissioning and removed afterwards. Usually marked "temporary" or "TS". No dedicated component; normally not modelled.
variants: Some legends use a dashed rectangle
Witch-hat strainers point the cone upstream

symbols.name: Steam trap
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A small circle on the line with "T" inside.
symbols.meaning: Lets condensate out of a steam line or tracer while holding steam back. Seen at the end of steam tracers and on steam-line drip legs. Becomes steam-trap.
variants: ISO-style legends draw a square on its corner with a filled dot
Some write "ST" next to a small square

symbols.name: Sight glass (sight flow indicator)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two concentric circles on the line (a viewing window).
symbols.meaning: In-line window to see that liquid is flowing: pump seal flush, lube oil, chemical injection. ISA calls it FG (flow glass). Becomes sight-glass.
variants: Some legends draw a circle with two short vertical bars
ISA style: a bubble with FG
A level gauge glass on a vessel is LG, not this

symbols.name: Restriction orifice
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ISA 5.1 (FO)
symbols.drawn: An orifice plate between two flange bars (a bar across the pipe with a gap in the middle), labelled "RO" or with an FO bubble.
symbols.meaning: Fixed plate that limits flow: after blowdown valves, on minimum-flow lines and on purge connections. It is not a meter, so there are no dp taps. Becomes restriction-orifice.
variants: Multi-stage ROs are drawn as several plates in series
Look-alike: orifice flow element (FE) has dp tap lines to a transmitter

symbols.name: Insulating joint (monolithic)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ISO 15589-1 (cathodic protection)
symbols.drawn: A short rectangle on the line with diagonal hatching inside, sometimes labelled "IJ".
symbols.meaning: Electrically isolates a pipeline (cathodic protection) from the plant. Seen on risers, export lines and at battery limits. Becomes insulating-joint.
variants: Insulating flange kits: a flange pair with a thick bar between them
Some legends draw two flange bars with a small gap

symbols.name: Drain funnel (tundish)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A drain line ending in the open, just above a V-shaped funnel that leads down to the open drain.
symbols.meaning: Open drain hub with a visible air break. It collects hydrocarbon-free or open drains into the open-drain system. Becomes drain-hub.
variants: Some legends draw a cup or a small triangle
Hazardous open drains must be sealed; look for a seal loop or a P-trap under it

symbols.name: Hose connection
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A small isolation valve on a branch that ends in a coupling (a short block with ridges), often marked "HC".
symbols.meaning: Utility hose connection (utility station: air, nitrogen, water or steam) or a flushing / steam-out connection. A utility station (several hose drops on one post) becomes utility-station; a lone hose connection is listed, not modelled.
variants: Quick-connect couplings may be drawn as a small triangle
Utility stations are often one symbol with a list of services

symbols.name: Vent with cap
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A short branch rising from the line with a small isolation valve and a cap (half-round) on top.
symbols.meaning: High-point vent for hydrotest and commissioning: valve plus cap or blind. Usually ¾" and not modelled.
variants: The end may carry a blind flange or a plug instead of a cap
Vents to atmosphere on hydrocarbon lines need a cap or plug, so check the line class

symbols.name: Drain with plug
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A short branch going down from the line with a small isolation valve and a solid plug (filled square) at the end.
symbols.meaning: Low-point drain for hydrotest and maintenance: valve plus plug. Usually ¾" and not modelled.
variants: Drains to the closed drain system are drawn connected to the CD header instead

symbols.name: Sample connection
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / ISA 5.1
symbols.drawn: A small branch from the line with a needle or isolation valve, ending in an open end over a small bottle; sometimes a box labelled "SC" or a sample cooler.
symbols.meaning: Manual sample point for lab analysis (oil-in-water, BS&W, H2S, glycol). Closed-loop samplers return to the process. Listed, not modelled.
variants: ISA style: a bubble with AX or SP
Closed sample systems are drawn as a box with in and return lines

symbols.name: Piping specification break
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A short bar across the line with the two piping class codes written on either side of it (e.g. A1A | D6A).
symbols.meaning: Where the piping class (material and pressure rating) changes, usually at a valve or a flange. Not a physical item, but it tells you the rating on each side. Use it for each line's spec.
variants: Some legends use a small diamond or a "Z" across the line
Often sits right next to the last valve rated for the higher class

symbols.name: Insulation mark
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A process line with thin dashed lines running parallel above and below it over the insulated length.
symbols.meaning: The line is insulated (heat conservation, personnel protection or cold). Most drawings show it only as the insulation code at the end of the line number, e.g. "-H" or "-PP". Set the line as insulated.
variants: Insulation codes: H heat conservation, C cold, PP personnel protection, AC acoustic, N none
Some legends hatch a short stretch of the line instead

symbols.name: Electric heat tracing mark
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A process line with a thin zig-zag (resistor-like) line running beside it, marked "ET".
symbols.meaning: Electrically traced line to stop freezing, waxing or hydrates. A tracing circuit and controller exist. Shown in the insulation code as "ET". Note it on the line; it is not modelled as geometry.
variants: Many legends draw a plain dashed line alongside with "ET"
Self-regulating vs constant-wattage cable is only on the heat-tracing isometrics

symbols.name: Steam tracing mark
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A process line with a thin dashed tracer line beside it, marked "ST", usually ending at a steam trap.
symbols.meaning: Steam- or hot-oil-traced line. Mostly onshore and in refineries; rare offshore. Note it on the line.
variants: Hot-water or glycol tracing: same, marked "WT" or "GT"
Jacketed lines are drawn differently (see the jacketed line)

symbols.name: Slope (fall) mark
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: The word "SLOPE" or a ratio (e.g. 1:100) with an arrow along the line pointing downhill.
symbols.meaning: The line must fall continuously in the arrow direction: drains, flare headers and relief lines (no pockets). Affects routing, not components. Keep runs level or falling towards the drum.
variants: Some legends use a small right triangle above the line
"No pockets" or "free draining" notes mean the same

symbols.name: Flow direction arrow
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A solid arrowhead on the line.
symbols.meaning: Direction of normal flow in the line. Use it to orient check valves and to decide which equipment is "from" and which is "to".
variants: Open-headed arrows are used for signal and relief flow on some legends

symbols.name: Line crossing (no connection)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: Two lines crossing, with one broken (a small gap either side of the other line), or with a small hop (semicircle) over it.
symbols.meaning: The lines cross on paper only and are not connected. Don't make a tee here.
variants: Convention: the vertical line is usually the one broken
Older drawings use a hop (semicircle)
A plain cross with no dot is ambiguous: treat it as no connection unless there is a dot

symbols.name: Line junction (tee)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A branch line meeting a run line in a T, with a solid dot at the junction.
symbols.meaning: Branch connection: a tee, or a welded branch fitting (olet). A welded branch outlet (weldolet, sockolet) becomes olet. In plant.json, model a tee with the tee component and connect the run ends and the branch port.
variants: The dot is often omitted on T junctions (a T cannot be a crossing)
Branch size may differ: reducing tee or olet

symbols.name: Injection quill / point
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A small branch entering the pipe (often after a check valve), with its end bent inside the pipe and pointing downstream.
symbols.meaning: Chemical injection point: corrosion inhibitor, scale inhibitor, methanol, demulsifier, biocide. The supply comes from the chemical injection package. Listed, not modelled; the package is chemical-injection-skid.
variants: Often drawn just as a small line ending in a dot or an arrow on the main line, with the chemical name
A check valve and a double block on the branch are typical

symbols.name: Corrosion probe / coupon
symbols.standard: Company legend practice (ISA-style bubble)
symbols.drawn: A short access fitting on top of the line with a small box or bubble marked "CP" (probe) or "CC" (coupon), and a probe tip into the flow.
symbols.meaning: Corrosion monitoring point: an ER/LPR probe or a weight-loss coupon in a high-pressure access fitting. Listed, not modelled.
variants: Legends vary: a diamond, a box or a circle with CC/CP/CE
Sand probes are drawn similarly, marked SP or SE

symbols.name: Vent to atmosphere (gooseneck)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 24-25, fittings and piping) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A line rising and turning back down at the top (a gooseneck or bent open end), sometimes with "ATM" written beside it.
symbols.meaning: Open vent to a safe location: instrument-air and nitrogen relief, tank vents and utility PSV outlets. For hydrocarbons, cold vents go to a vent stack instead.
variants: A plain open end with "TO ATM"
A mesh or bird screen may be drawn at the end

symbols.name: Main process line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A heavy (thick) solid line, with a line number written along it (e.g. 8"-PG-1101-D6A-N).
symbols.meaning: Main process pipe. Each one becomes a plant.json line between equipment ports or battery limits. Read size, service, sequence number, class and insulation from the line number.
variants: Line weight is the only difference from secondary lines; some CAD exports lose it
Line-number order differs by company (size-service-number-class-insulation is common)

symbols.name: Secondary / minor process or utility line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A medium-weight solid line, thinner than main process lines, with its own line number.
symbols.meaning: Utility, minor process or small-bore line: drains, vents, chemical injection, fuel gas, air. Model it if it is a numbered line between modelled items.
variants: Some companies draw utilities in a medium weight and instrument process connections thin

symbols.name: Future line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A heavy line made of long dashes, often marked "FUTURE".
symbols.meaning: Planned but not part of this scope. Do not model it; at most, leave a blinded tie-in.
variants: Some legends use a dash-dot line
Future equipment is drawn dashed too

symbols.name: Existing line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A screened (grey or lighter) line, sometimes labelled "EXISTING" or with a note, on brownfield drawings.
symbols.meaning: Existing pipe that this project does not change. Model it only if the existing plant is in scope.
variants: Monochrome prints may show existing lines as thin, or hatched, or with an "E" in the line number
Check the legend: some brownfield sets reverse this and screen the new work

symbols.name: Demolished / to be removed line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A line with short diagonal hatch marks (or crosses) along it, often labelled "TO BE REMOVED" or "DEMOLISH".
symbols.meaning: Pipe to be removed in this project. Do not model it.
variants: Some legends use × crosses (do not confuse with the thin capillary line)
Removed equipment is cross-hatched or crossed out

symbols.name: Instrument supply / process connection
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin solid line from a process line or vessel to an instrument bubble (or from a supply header).
symbols.meaning: Impulse line from the process to an instrument, or an instrument supply (air, power). It shows where the instrument is mounted. Not a numbered process line.
variants: ISA 5.1-2009 also uses a plain thin line for "undefined signal"
Supply type may be written on it: AS (air supply), ES (electric), NS (nitrogen), HS (hydraulic)

symbols.name: Pneumatic signal
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin line with pairs of short diagonal slashes (//) at intervals.
symbols.meaning: Air signal, e.g. from an I/P or positioner to an actuator, or an instrument-air signal to a pneumatic controller. Not modelled.
variants: Older drawings (ISA 1984) used the same // marks
Some legends use three slashes for electric (pre-1984)

symbols.name: Hydraulic signal
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin line with small "L" marks at intervals.
symbols.meaning: Hydraulic signal or power: wellhead control panel to SSV and SCSSV actuators, HPU lines. Not modelled, but it identifies hydraulic actuators.
variants: Hydraulic supply lines may also be drawn as process lines with the HYD service code

symbols.name: Electric signal
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin dashed line.
symbols.meaning: Analog (4-20 mA) or discrete electrical signal between instruments, DCS, PLC and SIS. It shows the loop, not a cable route. Not modelled.
variants: ISA 1984 drew electric signals as a dashed line too; very old drawings use ///
Some legends draw binary (on/off) electric signals with a different dash pattern

symbols.name: Capillary tube (filled system)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin line with small × marks at intervals.
symbols.meaning: Filled capillary: a thermal system bulb to its gauge or regulator, or a diaphragm seal to a transmitter. Part of the instrument; not modelled separately.
variants: Do not confuse with demolished lines (heavy, hatched) on brownfield drawings

symbols.name: Guided electromagnetic or sonic signal
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin solid line with small sine-wave marks on it at intervals.
symbols.meaning: Signal carried along a guide: fibre optic, or a guided-wave radar probe (signal down the rod). Not modelled.
variants: Some legends draw guided signals as a solid line with small loops
The exact mark varies between editions and company legends; check the legend

symbols.name: Unguided electromagnetic, radio or sonic signal
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A free sine wave with no straight line under it.
symbols.meaning: Wireless or through-the-air signal: radio and WirelessHART transmitters, non-contact radar, nuclear level gauges, light and sound. Not modelled.
variants: Wireless instruments may also be marked "W" or have an antenna mark on the bubble

symbols.name: Data link / software link
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin line with small open circles on it at intervals.
symbols.meaning: Internal system or communication link: software connections inside the DCS (e.g. a cascade setpoint) or a bus between systems (DCS to PLC, Modbus, fieldbus). Not modelled.
variants: ISA 5.1-2009 separates shared-system links from fieldbus links with different marks; many legends use filled dots or diamonds for fieldbus
Very old drawings: o-o-o meant "software or data link" only

symbols.name: Mechanical link
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (instrument line symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thin line with a small open circle at each end (pivots).
symbols.meaning: Mechanical connection between devices: a float to a valve, interlocked PSV changeover valves, or a key interlock. Not modelled; note the interlock.
variants: Legends differ: some draw a plain line with "MECH. LINK", others a dashed line with circles
Key interlocks are often shown as a dashed line with a key symbol or "KI"

symbols.name: Heat-traced line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A heavy process line with a thin dashed line running alongside it.
symbols.meaning: The process line is traced (electric or steam). The tracer type is in the insulation code (ET/ST) or a tag on the tracer. Set the line as insulated.
variants: See the electric and steam tracing marks for the lettered forms

symbols.name: Jacketed line
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 25) / PIP PIC001 (line conventions)
symbols.drawn: A heavy process line with a thin outer line on both sides, closed at the ends (a pipe inside a pipe).
symbols.meaning: Jacketed pipe: a heating medium flows in the outer jacket (sulphur, wax and heavy oil). Rare offshore. Model only the inner pipe and note the jacket.
variants: Some legends draw a double line only over the jacketed length

symbols.name: Off-page connector, outgoing
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: The line ends at the flat side of a pentagon (an arrow-shaped box) that points away in the flow direction. The destination drawing number and the service or equipment, e.g. "TO PID-102 / V-2100", are written inside or beside it (left blank here).
symbols.meaning: The line continues on another sheet. If that sheet is in the job, join the two halves into one line (same line number). Otherwise end the line at a battery limit in plant.json ({ at, label: "TO …" }).
variants: Some legends use an arrow with the text above, or a rectangle with an arrowhead
Instrument signals use smaller connectors, often a circle with a letter or a hexagon

symbols.name: Off-page connector, incoming
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A pentagon at the start of the line, pointing into the line in the flow direction, with "FROM PID-…" and the source text inside or beside it (left blank here).
symbols.meaning: The line comes from another sheet. Join it to the matching outgoing connector if that sheet is in scope; otherwise start the line at a battery limit ({ at, label: "FROM …" }).
variants: Some legends point both connector types to the right regardless of direction; read the TO/FROM text

symbols.name: Utility connector
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A small rounded box at a line end with the utility code inside (e.g. N2, IA, UA, PW, FG).
symbols.meaning: Utility supply or return from the utility distribution sheets, without the full off-page reference. End the line at a battery limit labelled with the utility.
variants: Some legends use an ellipse, a flag or a hexagon
Utility stations (hose connections) carry a list of codes

symbols.name: On-sheet continuation
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A line ending in an arrow at a small circle with a letter; the same letter appears where the line resumes on the same sheet.
symbols.meaning: The line jumps across the same drawing to avoid a long route. Treat both ends as one continuous line.
variants: A small circle with a letter can look like an instrument bubble; continuation letters are single letters and have no number

symbols.name: Tie-in point
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A bar across the line where new pipe joins existing pipe, with a leader to a hexagon or flag holding the tie-in number (e.g. TP-01).
symbols.meaning: Where new work connects to existing plant (hot-tap, cold cut, or flange break). In plant.json a tie-in is a battery limit: end the line with { at, label: "TIE-IN TP-01" }; it renders as a blinded end with a yellow band.
variants: Tie-in marks vary: hexagon, flag, circle with TI, or a diamond
Hot taps are often noted "HT"

symbols.name: Battery limit
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A long dash-dot boundary line crossing the pipe, labelled "B.L." or "BATTERY LIMIT", often with the scope owner written on each side.
symbols.meaning: The edge of the modelled scope. In plant.json the line's from/to becomes a BatteryLimit object { at: [x, y, z], direction?, label? } instead of "TAG.port". It renders as a blinded end with a yellow band and the label. No component.
variants: Some legends draw a heavy dashed line with a flag
Package (vendor) boundaries look similar but enclose equipment

symbols.name: Package / vendor scope boundary
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A dash-dot rectangle drawn around a group of equipment and piping, with the package tag and vendor written in a corner, and connections crossing its edge.
symbols.meaning: Everything inside is supplied as one package (skid), and its details may be on the vendor's P&IDs. Map the package to a package component (e.g. chemical-injection-skid, instrument-air-package) and the crossing lines to its ports.
variants: Some legends use long dashes or a double-dash-dot
Interface points on the boundary may carry small flags or "VI" (vendor interface) marks

symbols.name: Interlock / logic diamond
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009 (binary logic)
symbols.drawn: A diamond with "I" (or an interlock number) inside, with signal lines in and out.
symbols.meaning: Interlock or logic function, defined on the logic diagrams or the cause & effect chart: e.g. LAHH trips a pump and closes an ESDV. Not physical; use it to understand the shutdowns.
variants: The number inside refers to the logic or C&E sheet
ISA logic gates (AND/OR) may be drawn as boxes on the P&ID
SIS trips are often a diamond with "S" or "SIS"

symbols.name: Note reference
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A number inside a small hexagon (or a flag or box) with a leader to the item; the note itself is in the notes block.
symbols.meaning: Points to a drawing note: slopes, no pockets, vendor scope, minimum distances or hold items. Read the note; it often explains things the symbols cannot.
variants: Some companies use a flag or a circle; a hexagon with a number only is a note, while an ISA computer-function hexagon has tag letters

symbols.name: Hold / revision cloud
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A scalloped (cloud) outline around part of the drawing, often with "HOLD" or a revision triangle.
symbols.meaning: The clouded part is on hold (unconfirmed) or changed in this revision. Treat the data inside as provisional and list it as an assumption.
variants: Holds may be written "HOLD 3" with a hold list
Revision clouds are paired with a revision triangle

symbols.name: Revision marker
symbols.standard: PIP PIC001 / ISO 10628-1 (diagram rules) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A small triangle with a revision number or letter inside, next to a change (often inside a cloud).
symbols.meaning: Marks what changed in that revision. Check the revision block to see whether the change is approved.
variants: Some companies use a circle or hexagon for revisions

symbols.name: Field-mounted instrument (discrete)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A plain circle with no horizontal line, containing the tag letters and usually the loop number.
symbols.meaning: A discrete instrument mounted in the field, on or next to the pipe or vessel: transmitters, gauges, switches and local controllers. These are the bubbles that become physical instruments; read the letters to choose the component (PT → pressure-transmitter, PI → pressure-gauge, etc.).
variants: Bubble size varies; ISA suggests about 11 mm (7/16")
Wireless field instruments may carry a small antenna mark
Two touching circles = one device with two functions

symbols.name: Instrument in main control room (primary location)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A circle with one solid horizontal line across the middle; letters above the line, loop number below.
symbols.meaning: A discrete (hardwired) instrument or function in the main control room, normally accessible to the operator: a panel indicator, controller or push-button. It is not on the plot; don't model it, but it tells you which field instrument exists.
variants: On ISA 5.1-2009 drawings, solid bar = central/main control room
Circle-in-square with a bar = the same location but in the DCS

symbols.name: Instrument on local / auxiliary panel
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A circle with two parallel horizontal lines across the middle (a double bar).
symbols.meaning: Instrument or function on a secondary or local panel accessible to the operator: a local control panel, package panel or LER panel. Not on the plot; the package or panel may be modelled as a building or skid.
variants: ISA 5.1-2009: double solid bar = secondary/local panel, normally accessible; double dashed bar = local, not normally accessible
Older drawings (1984): double bar = auxiliary location

symbols.name: Instrument behind the panel (not accessible)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A circle with a dashed horizontal line across the middle.
symbols.meaning: Function not normally accessible to the operator: behind the panel, in a marshalling cabinet or rack room (relays, converters, signal isolators). Not modelled.
variants: Circle-in-square with a dashed bar = a DCS function not shown to the operator (internal calculation)

symbols.name: Shared display / shared control (DCS)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A circle inside a square, with a solid horizontal line across, letters above and loop number below.
symbols.meaning: A function in the basic process control system (BPCS/DCS) shown on operator screens: indication, control, alarms. Software, not hardware on the plot. A PIC-101 in the DCS implies a field PT-101.
variants: No bar = a field-mounted shared display (e.g. a local HMI)
Dashed bar = DCS function the operator cannot see
ISA 5.1-2009 redefined circle-in-square as the BPCS whatever the hardware

symbols.name: PLC / alternate control system function
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A diamond inside a square, with a horizontal line across when operator-accessible.
symbols.meaning: A function in a PLC or other non-BPCS control system: package PLCs, sequence logic, compressor UCP. Software, not modelled.
variants: ISA 5.1-2009 lets the user assign diamond-in-square to either "alternate control system" or SIS; the drawing legend says which
Some old sources describe a triangle-in-square for PLCs; the standard shape is the diamond

symbols.name: Safety instrumented system (SIS) function
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols) / IEC 61511
symbols.drawn: A diamond inside a square (with a bar when operator-accessible), carrying a trip function such as LSHH or PSHH. Many legends add "SIS" or a distinct colour or letter.
symbols.meaning: A trip or permissive in the safety instrumented system: PSD/ESD logic on independent SIL-rated hardware. Not physical. Each one implies dedicated field sensors (often LZT/PZT, or a second transmitter) and final elements (ESDV, BDV, motor trips).
variants: ISA 5.1-2009 introduced the diamond-in-square option for SIS. ISA describes the 2022 edition as a corrections release, and no change to this symbol was reported (the 2022 text was not checked)
Many operators mark SIS loops with Z (e.g. PZT, LZT, XZV) or a "S" prefix; this is company practice, not ISA
Some legends use a hexagon or a double-bordered diamond for the SIS and keep diamond-in-square for PLCs

symbols.name: Computer function
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A hexagon (pointed left and right), with a horizontal line across when operator-accessible.
symbols.meaning: A function on a separate computer (supervisory or optimisation system, advanced process control, flow computer software, historian calculation). Not modelled.
variants: A hexagon with only a number and no letters is a note marker, not a computer function
Flow computers on metering skids are often drawn this way, with FQ

symbols.name: Multi-function instrument (touching bubbles)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: Two bubbles drawn touching side by side, each with its own letters, e.g. PIT and PSHH.
symbols.meaning: One physical device performing two functions (e.g. a transmitter with a built-in switch), or two functions in one housing. Model one instrument.
variants: Bubbles of different shapes may touch (a field device with its DCS function)

symbols.name: Function block (computing / signal conversion)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: A small square drawn beside a bubble (usually a Y relay or compute bubble) containing a math or conversion symbol: √, Σ, ×, ÷, I/P, f(x), >, <.
symbols.meaning: What the Y function does: square-root extraction (√), totalising (Σ), high or low select (> <), conversion (I/P). Not physical.
variants: Some legends put the symbol inside the bubble instead

symbols.name: Alarm and trip annotation
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (general instrument and function symbols)
symbols.drawn: Small letters next to a bubble: H, HH, L, LL (or AH, AHH, AL, ALL), sometimes with a setpoint value.
symbols.meaning: The loop has alarms (H/L) or trips (HH/LL) at those points. HH and LL usually drive the cause & effect matrix. Not physical; record them as instrument alarm limits.
variants: ISA succeeding letters: A = alarm, S = switch/trip; H, L, M = high, low, middle
Trips are often in the SIS bubble (e.g. LSHH) instead of annotations

symbols.name: ISA 5.1 identification letters
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (Table 4.1, identification letters)
symbols.drawn: Tag letters inside any bubble, e.g. "FIC" over "101": first letter = measured variable, following letters = functions.
symbols.meaning: FIRST LETTER (measured or initiating variable, with optional modifier): A analysis, B burner/combustion, C user's choice (often conductivity), D user's choice (often density), E voltage, F flow (modifier F ratio), G user's choice (often gauging/position), H hand, I current, J power, K time/schedule, L level, M user's choice (often moisture), N user's choice, O user's choice, P pressure/vacuum, Q quantity (modifier Q integrate/totalise), R radiation, S speed/frequency (modifier: S safety), T temperature, U multivariable, V vibration/machinery analysis, W weight/force, X unclassified, Y event/state/presence, Z position/dimension. First-letter modifiers: D differential, F ratio, J scan, K time rate of change, Q integrate/totalise, S safety, X/Y/Z axis. SUCCEEDING LETTERS: A alarm, B user's choice, C control, D differential (modifier), E sensor/primary element, G glass/gauge/viewing device, H high, I indicate, K control station, L light or low, M middle/momentary, N user's choice, O orifice/restriction, P point (test connection), Q integrate, R record, S switch, T transmit, U multifunction, V valve/damper/louvre, W well (thermowell), X unclassified, Y relay/compute/convert, Z driver/actuator/final control element. Examples: PT pressure transmitter, PDT differential-pressure transmitter, FE flow element, FIC flow indicating controller, LSHH level switch high-high, TW thermowell, PSV pressure safety valve, XV on/off valve, HS hand switch, ZSO position switch open, AT analyser transmitter, FQ totaliser, LG level gauge.
variants: Company standards fill the user's-choice letters differently (C, D, G, M, N, O)
Some companies put Z after the first letter for SIS loops (PZT); that is not ISA
Loop numbers may include an area or unit prefix, e.g. 20-PT-1101

symbols.name: Orifice plate flow element with dp transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An orifice plate between a flange pair on the line (a bar across the pipe with a gap in the middle for the bore), with two impulse lines from the flange taps up to an FT bubble.
symbols.meaning: Differential-pressure flow measurement. FE is the plate in its orifice-flange pair and FT is the dp cell. Fiscal and allocation meters, gas flow to flare and fuel. Model one item (orifice-flowmeter) for the FE+FT pair.
variants: Simplified form: two short bars across the line with an FE bubble
A restriction orifice (RO) looks the same but has no taps
Orifice fittings (senior / dual-chamber) are drawn as a box labelled with the type

symbols.name: Venturi tube
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: The line narrows through a short throat and widens again (converging and diverging lines either side of the pipe), with an FE bubble above.
symbols.meaning: Low-loss dp flow element for large water and gas lines and multiphase meters (venturi + gamma). No dedicated component; orifice-flowmeter is the nearest dp meter.
variants: Some legends draw it as a box with "V"
Multiphase flow meters (MPFM) combine a venturi with a gamma densitometer box
