symbols.name: Flow nozzle
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A flange pair with two curved lines inside the pipe converging downstream (the nozzle profile), and an FE bubble.
symbols.meaning: Dp flow element for high-velocity steam and gas. No dedicated component.
variants: Often just a box with "FN" or the same symbol as an orifice with "NOZZLE"

symbols.name: Pitot tube
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A probe from an FE bubble into the pipe, bent into an L whose open end faces upstream.
symbols.meaning: Point-velocity flow probe. Rare on process lines, used for testing and ducts. No dedicated component.
variants: Some legends draw a small open-ended hook symbol without a bubble

symbols.name: Averaging pitot (multiport probe)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A bar across the full pipe bore with several small holes (dots) on its upstream face, under an FE bubble.
symbols.meaning: Multi-port averaging pitot (Annubar type). Used on large gas lines and flare headers because the pressure loss is low. No dedicated component.
variants: Often drawn like a pitot tube with "AVG" or the vendor name

symbols.name: Electromagnetic flowmeter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An in-line rectangle on the pipe with "M" inside, under an FT/FIT bubble.
symbols.meaning: Magnetic flowmeter for conductive liquids only: seawater, produced water, water injection, chemicals. Not for hydrocarbons or gas. Becomes magnetic-flowmeter.
variants: Some legends write "MAG" or draw two coil arcs either side of the pipe

symbols.name: Vortex flowmeter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An in-line rectangle with a small triangle (the bluff body) and a wavy vortex trail behind it, under an FT bubble.
symbols.meaning: Vortex-shedding meter for steam, gas and clean liquids: utilities, fuel gas, instrument air. Becomes vortex-flowmeter.
variants: Some legends write "VOR" or "VORTEX" in the box

symbols.name: Turbine flowmeter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An in-line rectangle with a small rotor (a hub with blades) inside, under an FT or FQ bubble.
symbols.meaning: Turbine meter for clean light liquids: fiscal oil metering (with a prover), diesel, chemicals. No single-meter component; fiscal runs are metering-skid.
variants: Some legends write "T" or "TUR" in the box
Helical turbine meters on fiscal skids are drawn the same

symbols.name: Positive displacement flowmeter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An in-line rectangle with two small touching ovals or circles (meshing rotors) inside, often with an FQ (totaliser) bubble.
symbols.meaning: Oval-gear or rotary PD meter for viscous liquids, chemical dosing and diesel transfer. Counts volume directly. No dedicated component.
variants: Some legends write "PD" in the box

symbols.name: Ultrasonic flowmeter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two small transducers on opposite sides of the pipe, offset along it, with a dashed diagonal sound path between them, under an FT bubble.
symbols.meaning: Transit-time ultrasonic meter: fiscal gas metering (multipath), flare gas and large liquid lines. Becomes ultrasonic-flowmeter.
variants: Some legends draw a box with "US" or "UT"
Clamp-on meters are drawn outside the pipe wall

symbols.name: Coriolis mass flowmeter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An in-line box on the pipe with a looped (U-shaped) tube inside, under an FT bubble.
symbols.meaning: Coriolis mass meter: condensate, oil allocation, chemicals and LACT/fiscal liquid service. It measures density too. Becomes coriolis-flowmeter.
variants: Some legends write "C" or "CORIOLIS" or "MASS" in the box

symbols.name: Variable-area flowmeter (rotameter)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A vertical tapered tube, wider at the top, with a small float inside; the flow enters at the bottom and leaves at the top.
symbols.meaning: Local flow indicator for purge gas, small utilities, seal flush and chemical injection. No dedicated component; usually not modelled.
variants: ISA style: an FI bubble on the line with "VA" or "ROTA"
Metal-tube rotameters with transmitters are tagged FIT

symbols.name: Thermowell with temperature element / transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A U-shaped pocket dipping into the line (the thermowell), with a line up to a TT or TE bubble.
symbols.meaning: Temperature measurement: a thermowell (TW), an element (TE, an RTD or thermocouple) and a transmitter (TT). Model one temperature-transmitter for the loop.
variants: Some legends draw the well as a short line into the pipe with a dot
A test thermowell (TW only, no TE) is for a portable probe; skip it

symbols.name: Local temperature gauge
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A thermowell (U-shaped pocket in the line) with a TI bubble on it.
symbols.meaning: Bimetallic dial thermometer in a thermowell, read locally. Becomes temperature-gauge.
variants: Tagged TG on some legends
A dial (circle with a pointer) is sometimes drawn instead of a bubble

symbols.name: Local pressure gauge
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A PI (or PG) bubble on a thin impulse line from the pipe, often with a small root or isolation valve on the impulse line.
symbols.meaning: Bourdon-tube dial gauge read locally: pump discharges, filters and vessels. Becomes pressure-gauge.
variants: ISA tag is PI; many companies use PG
A gauge with a seal or snubber shows extra small symbols on the impulse line

symbols.name: Pressure transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A PT (or PIT) bubble on a thin impulse line from the pipe or vessel, with an electric (dashed) signal leaving to the DCS.
symbols.meaning: Electronic pressure transmitter feeding the DCS or SIS. Becomes pressure-transmitter.
variants: SIS transmitters are often PZT or carry an "S" suffix
Multivariable transmitters on flow loops may be tagged FT with P and T inputs

symbols.name: Differential pressure transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A PDT bubble with two impulse lines: one to each side of a filter, strainer, exchanger or column section.
symbols.meaning: Differential pressure across equipment: filter or strainer fouling, scrubber dp, column flooding. Becomes dp-transmitter.
variants: A local dp gauge is PDI or PDG
Dp level transmitters are tagged LT (see the dp level entry)

symbols.name: Pressure switch
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A bubble with PSH, PSL, PSHH or PSLL on an impulse line from the process.
symbols.meaning: Pressure switch giving a discrete alarm or trip. Old-style or package protection. Becomes pressure-switch.
variants: On modern plants the same letters often mean a trip point inside the DCS/SIS from a transmitter; then the bubble has a bar or a square
Packaged machines (lube oil, seal gas) still use real switches

symbols.name: Level gauge glass
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A tall narrow rectangle beside the vessel, joined to it by two horizontal nozzles (top and bottom), with an LG bubble.
symbols.meaning: Reflex or transparent sight glass showing the level directly. Common on older plant; many operators now use magnetic gauges, which are tagged LG too. No separate component; magnetic-level-gauge is the closest.
variants: Stacked or overlapping glasses are drawn as two or three offset rectangles
Look-alike: magnetic level gauge (chamber with a float and a flag indicator)

symbols.name: Magnetic level gauge
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A chamber beside the vessel on two nozzles, with a float inside and a column of indicator flaps (half-filled marks) on its face, and an LG bubble.
symbols.meaning: Float-and-magnet level indicator on a bypass chamber, readable from a distance. Often carries a level transmitter too. Becomes magnetic-level-gauge.
variants: Often drawn exactly like a gauge glass and tagged LG; the datasheet tells them apart
A clamp-on magnetostrictive LT on the chamber is drawn as a separate LT bubble

symbols.name: Displacer level transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An external cage beside the vessel on two nozzles, with a long slender displacer hanging inside from a torque tube at the top, and an LT bubble.
symbols.meaning: Buoyancy (displacer) level or interface transmitter. Classic on separators for oil/water interface. No dedicated component; model it as a level transmitter note on the vessel.
variants: Internal displacers (inside the vessel) are drawn as the displacer inside the vessel outline
Interface service may be tagged LDT or LT with "INTERFACE"

symbols.name: Differential pressure level transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An LT bubble with two impulse lines to the vessel: one from a low nozzle (high side) and one from a high nozzle (low side). Remote seals are drawn as capillaries (line with × marks).
symbols.meaning: Level from hydrostatic head: the most common level transmitter on separators and drums. Becomes dp-transmitter; the bubble letters (LT) give the service.
variants: With diaphragm seals the lines carry × marks (capillaries)
Bubble-tube (purge) level measurement looks similar with a purge supply

symbols.name: Guided wave radar level transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An LT bubble on a vessel-top (or chamber-top) nozzle, with a straight rod or cable probe running down into the liquid.
symbols.meaning: Guided wave radar: a pulse travels down the probe and reflects at the surface or interface. Separators, drums and bridles. Becomes guided-wave-radar.
variants: Often mounted in an external chamber (bridle), drawn like a displacer cage with a probe
Some legends mark it "GWR" beside the bubble

symbols.name: Non-contact radar level transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An LT bubble on a vessel-top nozzle, with a cone (horn antenna) pointing down and wave arcs (unguided signal) towards the liquid.
symbols.meaning: Free-space radar for tanks and sumps: storage tanks, open drains and caissons. No dedicated component; guided-wave-radar is the closest stand-in.
variants: Ultrasonic level transmitters are drawn the same and marked "US"

symbols.name: Nuclear (gamma) level transmitter
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A source holder (small box) on one side of the vessel and a detector rod on the other, joined by a wavy (radiation) line across the vessel, with an LT bubble on the detector.
symbols.meaning: Gamma level or density measurement through the vessel wall: slug catchers, desanders, profilers in separators. Needs radiation controls. No dedicated component.
variants: The source holder may be marked with the radiation trefoil or "RS"
Density profilers have many detectors in a vertical row

symbols.name: Vibrating fork level switch
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A short side nozzle into the vessel with two small prongs (the fork) inside, and an LS bubble (LSH, LSHH…) outside.
symbols.meaning: Point level switch for high or low alarms and trips, independent of the transmitter. Becomes level-switch.
variants: Many legends draw just the LSHH bubble on the vessel without the fork
Capacitance and float switches use the same bubble letters

symbols.name: Float level switch
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A float (circle) on a short arm inside the vessel, pivoted at the wall, with an LS bubble outside.
symbols.meaning: Mechanical float switch: sumps, drain drums, day tanks and lube-oil reservoirs. No dedicated component; level-switch is the nearest stand-in.
variants: Cage-mounted float switches sit in an external chamber like a displacer

symbols.name: Analyser (with sample probe)
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An AT (or AE) bubble linked to a probe that dips into the line, with the measured component written beside the bubble (O2, H2S, H2O, OIW, BS&W, CO2…).
symbols.meaning: Online analyser: water dew point, H2S, oxygen, oil-in-water, BS&W or water-cut. In-line probes sit on the pipe; extractive analysers have a sample line to an analyser shelter (analyser-shelter). No single component for the probe.
variants: The analyte is written beside the bubble, not as part of the tag
Extractive systems show a sample line, conditioning box and return
Gas chromatographs on metering skids are AT with "GC"

symbols.name: Diaphragm (remote) seal with capillary
symbols.standard: ISA 5.1-2009/2022 (primary element symbols) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A small flat seal on the pipe or vessel nozzle (a short rectangle with a curved diaphragm line), joined to a transmitter bubble by a capillary (a line with × marks).
symbols.meaning: Remote seal protecting a transmitter from corrosive, viscous or hot process fluid. Part of the transmitter; model the transmitter only.
variants: Some legends write "DS" or "SEAL" beside the instrument

symbols.name: Vertical vessel
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A tall rectangle with rounded (dished) top and bottom heads, with nozzles: inlet on the side, gas at the top, liquid at the bottom. Equipment tag and design data written beside it.
symbols.meaning: Vertical pressure vessel: scrubber, KO drum, flash drum or receiver. Gas/liquid duty with small liquid volume becomes vertical-separator; an air or nitrogen receiver becomes air-receiver. Read the title and service.
variants: ISO 10628-2 shows support skirt, legs or brackets as extra marks under the vessel
Internals (mesh pad, vane pack, inlet device) are often drawn inside
Jacketed or insulated vessels have hatching or a second outline

symbols.name: Vertical scrubber with mist eliminator
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A vertical vessel with a band near the top filled with a zig-zag or cross-hatch (the mesh pad or vane pack) and an inlet on the side below it.
symbols.meaning: Gas scrubber or KO drum: compressor suction scrubbers, fuel-gas scrubbers, inlet KO drums. Becomes vertical-separator with mesh or vane internals.
variants: Vane packs may be drawn as vertical zig-zags
Cyclonic internals are drawn as small cones
Filter-separators are horizontal with cartridges, see separation

symbols.name: Horizontal vessel
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A long horizontal rectangle with rounded heads at both ends, with nozzles on the top and bottom.
symbols.meaning: Horizontal drum: two-phase separator, surge drum, KO drum or drain drum. Becomes horizontal-separator (set the service: 2-phase, 3-phase or KO).
variants: Saddle supports are drawn as small trapezoids underneath
A horizontal vessel on saddles holding LPG is a bullet (see tank-bullet)

symbols.name: Three-phase separator (with boot and weir)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A horizontal vessel with a small vertical boot under it (a short rectangle), and an upright weir plate inside towards the outlet end. Separate oil and water outlets.
symbols.meaning: Oil/gas/water separator: HP and LP production separators, test separators. Water settles into the boot or before the weir, and oil spills over the weir into the oil bucket. Becomes horizontal-separator with service 3-phase.
variants: Some have no boot: interface level is held with a weir and separate oil and water outlets
Bucket-and-weir layouts show two plates
Inlet device, mesh pad and vortex breakers may also be drawn

symbols.name: Trayed column
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001 (X8101 tray column)
symbols.drawn: A tall vertical vessel with dished heads and short horizontal lines inside that alternate from left to right (the trays).
symbols.meaning: Tray column: stabilisers, TEG contactors, amine contactors and fractionators. Becomes column (trayed).
variants: ISO draws trays as dashed horizontal lines
Tray numbers are written at feed and draw-off points
Bubble-cap and valve trays have small caps or marks on the tray lines

symbols.name: Packed column
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001 (X8015 fixed bed)
symbols.drawn: A tall vertical vessel with one or more rectangles crossed corner to corner (an X), the packed beds, each with a short distributor line above it.
symbols.meaning: Packed column: structured or random packing for TEG contactors, strippers and scrubbers. Becomes column (packed).
variants: Beds may be drawn as dotted or hatched areas
An X box is also the ISO symbol for a fixed catalyst or adsorbent bed; read the service

symbols.name: Cone-roof storage tank
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001 (X2063 conical roof, flat bottom)
symbols.drawn: A wide flat-bottomed rectangle with a shallow pointed (conical) roof.
symbols.meaning: Atmospheric storage tank (API 650): diesel, water, produced water, slop or crude storage. Becomes storage-tank.
variants: A breather valve and flame arrester are usually drawn on the roof
Insulated or heated tanks show hatching or coils

symbols.name: Dome-roof storage tank
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001 (X8200 dished roof)
symbols.drawn: A wide flat-bottomed rectangle with a curved (domed) roof.
symbols.meaning: Atmospheric or low-pressure tank with a self-supporting dome roof. Becomes storage-tank.
variants: Geodesic aluminium domes over floating-roof tanks are drawn as a dome with the floating roof inside

symbols.name: Floating-roof tank
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A flat-bottomed tank with an open top and a horizontal deck floating inside below the rim, often with a rolling ladder drawn diagonally from the rim to the deck.
symbols.meaning: External floating-roof tank (API 650 Annex C) for crude and volatile products: the roof rides on the liquid to cut vapour losses. Becomes storage-tank.
variants: Internal floating roofs are drawn inside a cone or dome roof
The roof drain (articulated) is drawn as a pipe from the deck to the shell

symbols.name: Spherical tank (sphere)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001 (2063 / X8010 spherical vessel)
symbols.drawn: A circle standing on vertical legs.
symbols.meaning: Pressurised sphere for LPG, butane or NGL storage. Becomes spherical-tank.
variants: ISO draws a plain circle for "spherical vessel" and adds legs for "on legs"

symbols.name: Bullet tank (horizontal pressure storage)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 1-2, vessels, tanks and columns) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A horizontal vessel with rounded heads standing on two saddles, sometimes inside a mound (a hump of earth).
symbols.meaning: Horizontal pressure storage for LPG, propane or NGL. Becomes bullet-tank. It looks like a horizontal drum; tell them apart by the tag and service.
variants: Mounded bullets are drawn under a curved earth line

symbols.name: Caisson (sump / pump caisson)
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A long vertical tube hanging down from the deck through the sea surface (a wavy line), open at the bottom.
symbols.meaning: Deck-hung caisson: seawater lift and firewater pump caissons, open drain and produced-water disposal caissons. Becomes caisson.
variants: Pump caissons show a vertical turbine or submersible pump inside
Disposal caissons show the inlet near the top and an open end

symbols.name: Slug catcher (finger type)
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Several long parallel pipes (fingers) joined at the inlet end by a manifold, with gas risers at the inlet end and a liquid header at the far end.
symbols.meaning: Pipeline slug catcher at an onshore terminal: the fingers store liquid slugs and the gas leaves from the top. Becomes slug-catcher.
variants: Vessel-type slug catchers are drawn as a large horizontal drum

symbols.name: Heat exchanger (general)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA (X8079)
symbols.drawn: A circle with a zig-zag line passing through it (one fluid) and pipe stubs on the circle (the other fluid).
symbols.meaning: Any heat exchanger, drawn generically (common on PFDs and simplified P&IDs). Usually a shell-and-tube unit, so map it to shell-and-tube-exchanger unless the title, tag or datasheet says plate, air-cooled or hairpin.
variants: ISO 10628-2 also uses it for "condenser"
Some legends draw two concentric circles or a circle with a horizontal coil

symbols.name: Shell-and-tube exchanger, fixed tubesheet (BEM)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA
symbols.drawn: A horizontal shell with a rounded bonnet at each end and straight tube lines running the full length between two tubesheets.
symbols.meaning: Fixed-tubesheet exchanger (TEMA BEM/NEN): cheap and tight, but the tube bundle can't be pulled, so it is used for clean shell-side fluid. Becomes shell-and-tube-exchanger (temaType BEM).
variants: Simplified legends draw just a rectangle with a zig-zag tube line
An expansion bellows on the shell means a large thermal difference

symbols.name: Shell-and-tube exchanger, U-tube (BEU / AEU)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA
symbols.drawn: A horizontal shell with a channel head at one end only, a rounded shell cover at the other, and tube lines drawn as a U bending back.
symbols.meaning: U-tube exchanger: one tubesheet, removable bundle, takes thermal expansion. High-pressure gas coolers and heaters. Becomes shell-and-tube-exchanger (temaType AEU/BEU).
variants: The U may be drawn as one hairpin line

symbols.name: Shell-and-tube exchanger, floating head (AES)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA
symbols.drawn: A horizontal shell with a flat channel cover at one end and a larger domed shell cover at the other; inside the cover, a small floating-head arc closes the straight tubes.
symbols.meaning: Floating-head exchanger (TEMA AES/AET): removable bundle and free expansion, for dirty or fouling service such as crude coolers. Becomes shell-and-tube-exchanger (temaType AES).
variants: Often simplified to the fixed-tubesheet symbol with "AES" written beside it

symbols.name: Kettle reboiler
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA (TEMA K shell)
symbols.drawn: A small channel and tube bundle at one end, with the shell swelling into a much larger diameter over the bundle (a kettle), a weir plate at the far end, and a vapour outlet on top.
symbols.meaning: Kettle (TEMA K) reboiler or vaporiser: liquid boils around the bundle, vapour leaves the top and liquid spills over the weir. Glycol regeneration, propane chillers. Map to shell-and-tube-exchanger and note the kettle shell.
variants: Thermosyphon reboilers are drawn as vertical shell-and-tube exchangers beside the column

symbols.name: Condenser
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA
symbols.drawn: A shell-and-tube exchanger with a large vapour inlet on top, a small condensate outlet (often from a boot or hotwell) underneath, and cooling medium through the tube side.
symbols.meaning: Shell-side condenser: overhead condensers, regeneration still condensers. Same hardware as a shell-and-tube unit, so map it to shell-and-tube-exchanger (or air-cooled-exchanger if drawn with a fan).
variants: ISO 10628-2 uses the general exchanger symbol for condensers
Air-cooled condensers are drawn as an air cooler

symbols.name: Plate heat exchanger
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA
symbols.drawn: A rectangle (frame) with many thin vertical lines inside (the plates) and four connections, usually all on one end plate.
symbols.meaning: Gasketed or welded plate exchanger: compact cooling-medium/seawater coolers, TEG coolers. Becomes plate-heat-exchanger.
variants: Some legends draw a rectangle with a diagonal zig-zag
Printed-circuit (diffusion-bonded) exchangers are drawn as a solid block, which is a different component (printed-circuit-heat-exchanger)

symbols.name: Air-cooled exchanger (fin-fan)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA / API 661
symbols.drawn: A long horizontal bundle (a rectangle with a zig-zag or straight tube passes) with header boxes at the ends and a fan (a circle with blades) beside or under it, often with an M motor.
symbols.meaning: Fin-fan cooler: compressor discharge coolers, lube-oil and condensate coolers onshore. Becomes air-cooled-exchanger.
variants: Forced draught: fan below; induced draught: fan above
Louvres and VFD drives are drawn as extra marks
Some legends draw a rectangle with an X and a fan circle

symbols.name: Double-pipe (hairpin) exchanger
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA
symbols.drawn: A U-shaped (hairpin) pipe drawn as a pipe within a pipe: an inner line running through an outer annulus around the bend.
symbols.meaning: Hairpin or double-pipe exchanger: small duties at high pressure, sample coolers, small gas coolers. Becomes hairpin-exchanger.
variants: Simplified: two concentric lines with in and out arrows

symbols.name: Fired heater
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA (group 4) / API 560
symbols.drawn: A tall box (radiant section) with burners (small flames or triangles) along the floor, a narrower convection box above, and a tapered stack on top. A coil (zig-zag) runs through.
symbols.meaning: Direct-fired process heater: hot-oil heaters, glycol reboilers, crude heaters (mostly onshore). Becomes fired-heater.
variants: Simplified: a rectangle with a flame triangle under it
Box vs cylindrical heaters look similar on P&IDs

symbols.name: Electric heater
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA (X2070 electrical heating)
symbols.drawn: A horizontal vessel with a heating element drawn as a zig-zag (resistor) inside, and a terminal box at one end.
symbols.meaning: Electric process heater: fuel-gas superheaters, regeneration-gas heaters, start-up heaters. Becomes electric-heater.
variants: ISO 10628-2 shows a small resistor rectangle on the vessel side
Some legends write "EH" or "ELECTRIC" inside

symbols.name: Cooling tower
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 3-5, heat exchangers, furnaces, cooling towers) / PIP PIC001 / TEMA (group 5)
symbols.drawn: A tapering box with a fan on top (induced draught), water spray or fill inside, and a basin at the bottom.
symbols.meaning: Evaporative cooling tower for the onshore cooling-water system. Becomes cooling-tower.
variants: Natural-draught towers are drawn as a hyperbolic outline
Fan below = forced draught

symbols.name: Centrifugal pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A circle with the suction at the centre of one side and the discharge leaving tangentially from the top, standing on a small base. Often a small triangle inside points towards the discharge (drawn here).
symbols.meaning: Horizontal centrifugal pump: the default process and utility pump. Becomes centrifugal-pump (API 610 OH2); use between-bearings-pump for multistage BB units and vertical-inline-pump for OH3 when the datasheet says so.
variants: Some legends omit the inner triangle; ISO-style legends may draw a "V" from the suction side instead
The driver (M) may be drawn joined by a shaft line
Spared pumps A/B are drawn twice

symbols.name: Vertical in-line pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A pump circle with suction and discharge on the same horizontal line (in-line), and a motor box (M) mounted directly above it.
symbols.meaning: Close-coupled vertical in-line pump (API 610 OH3/OH4): cooling medium, chemicals, small duties. Becomes vertical-inline-pump.
variants: Often drawn as an ordinary centrifugal pump with a note "vertical in-line"

symbols.name: Vertical turbine (caisson) pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A motor on top of a discharge head on the deck, with a long column running down into a caisson or sump and a stack of bowls (stages) and a suction bell at the bottom, below the water line.
symbols.meaning: Line-shaft vertical turbine pump (API 610 VS1): seawater lift and firewater pumps on caissons. Becomes vertical-turbine-pump.
variants: Diesel-driven firewater versions have DE instead of M (see the fire pump)
Simplified: a centrifugal pump symbol with a long dip pipe

symbols.name: Submersible pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A capsule (pump and motor in one) at the bottom of a caisson or sump, below the water line, hanging from its discharge pipe; the power cable runs up beside it.
symbols.meaning: Electric submersible pump: seawater lift caissons, open-drain and sump pumps. Becomes submersible-pump.
variants: Some legends draw a centrifugal pump circle inside a sump outline with "SUB"

symbols.name: Reciprocating (plunger) pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A cylinder (rectangle) with a piston or plunger (T shape) inside, connected to a crank circle, with suction and discharge connections on the cylinder head.
symbols.meaning: Positive displacement plunger pump (API 674): high-pressure injection, glycol circulation, mud pumps and pigging. Becomes reciprocating-pump (use mud-pump for drilling mud pumps).
variants: ISO draws a circle with a piston mark inside
Pulsation dampeners and a relief valve on the discharge are usually drawn nearby

symbols.name: Gear pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A rounded casing with two meshing gears (two touching circles) inside, suction on one side and discharge on the other.
symbols.meaning: Rotary positive displacement pump: lube oil, fuel oil and chemical transfer. No dedicated component; usually part of a package.
variants: Some legends draw a pump circle with two small circles inside
Look-alike: PD flowmeter (smaller, on the line, with an FQ bubble)

symbols.name: Screw pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A long casing with a helical screw (a zig-zag along the axis) inside, suction underneath and discharge on top, with a drive shaft out of one end.
symbols.meaning: Twin or triple screw pump: crude transfer, lube oil, multiphase boosting. No dedicated component.
variants: Multiphase twin-screw pumps carry an "MPP" note

symbols.name: Metering (dosing) pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001 / API 675
symbols.drawn: A pump circle with an internal triangle and a long diagonal arrow through it (adjustable capacity); diaphragm heads may be drawn as a curved line inside.
symbols.meaning: Diaphragm or plunger metering pump (API 675): chemical injection, methanol, corrosion inhibitor. Usually part of the chemical injection package. Becomes metering-pump.
variants: Some legends write "MP" or draw a diaphragm arc on the head
Multi-head pumps are drawn as several circles on one driver

symbols.name: Progressive cavity pump
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (group 15, liquid pumps) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A long horizontal casing with a single sine-shaped rotor inside, suction at one end on top and discharge at the other end, often with a motor box.
symbols.meaning: Single-screw (Moineau) pump: sludge, oily water, drain sump and polymer duties. Becomes progressive-cavity-pump.
variants: Some legends draw a box with a helix and "PCP"

symbols.name: Centrifugal compressor
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A trapezoid lying on its side: wide at the suction end, narrow at the discharge end, with a shaft line to the driver.
symbols.meaning: Centrifugal (turbo) compressor (API 617): export, booster, flash-gas and recompression. Becomes centrifugal-compressor; a gas-turbine-driven train is gas-turbine-compressor.
variants: Multi-stage casings may show several trapezoids on one shaft
Anti-surge recycle (FV with UIC/FIC) and dry gas seals are drawn around it
Look-alike: a turbine trapezoid widens in the flow direction

symbols.name: Reciprocating compressor
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A cylinder rectangle with a double-acting piston inside, joined by a rod to a crank circle, with suction on top and discharge underneath each cylinder.
symbols.meaning: Reciprocating compressor (API 618): instrument air, fuel-gas boosting, high-pressure small flows. Becomes reciprocating-compressor (instrument-air packages become instrument-air-package).
variants: Each stage cylinder may be drawn separately with pulsation bottles
It looks like a reciprocating pump; the tag (K) and the service decide

symbols.name: Screw compressor
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A casing containing two meshing helical rotors (two zig-zags side by side), with suction and discharge connections and a shaft to the driver.
symbols.meaning: Rotary screw compressor (API 619): instrument and utility air, flash gas and vapour recovery. Becomes screw-compressor.
variants: Some legends draw the centrifugal trapezoid with "SCREW" written beside it
Oil-injected packages show an oil separator vessel downstream

symbols.name: Axial compressor
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A long trapezoid narrowing in the flow direction with rows of short vertical lines inside (the blade rows), and a shaft.
symbols.meaning: Axial-flow compressor: large air or gas flows, mainly as the compressor section of a gas turbine. As a separate machine it is rare offshore. No dedicated component.
variants: Usually seen only as part of the gas-turbine symbol

symbols.name: Blower / centrifugal fan
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 (group 17)
symbols.drawn: A circle (the scroll) with the outlet leaving tangentially as a short rectangular duct, and curved blades (or a small fan wheel) drawn inside.
symbols.meaning: Centrifugal fan or blower: HVAC supply and extract, combustion air, purge air. Becomes centrifugal-fan.
variants: Axial fans are drawn as a circle with a propeller
Positive displacement (roots) blowers are drawn as a circle with two lobes

symbols.name: Ejector / eductor
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 (jet pump)
symbols.drawn: A converging nozzle inside a body that narrows to a throat and then widens (diffuser): the motive fluid enters at the nozzle end, suction comes in from the side, and the mixture leaves at the wide end.
symbols.meaning: Jet pump with no moving parts: gas ejectors for low-pressure flash gas recovery, water eductors for sand jetting and drains. No dedicated component.
variants: Some legends draw two triangles (nozzle and diffuser) tip to tip with a side branch

symbols.name: Turbo-expander (expander-compressor)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two trapezoids on one shaft: the expander widens in the flow direction and the compressor narrows, back to back.
symbols.meaning: Expander drives a compressor from the energy of a gas pressure drop (NGL recovery, dew-pointing). No dedicated component.
variants: A generator-loaded expander has a G circle instead of the compressor

symbols.name: Gas turbine
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 (group 20)
symbols.drawn: A compressor trapezoid (narrowing), a small combustor circle, and a turbine trapezoid (widening), on a common shaft, with air in and exhaust out.
symbols.meaning: Gas turbine driver (API 616). Not modelled alone: with a generator it becomes gas-turbine-generator, and with a compressor it becomes gas-turbine-compressor.
variants: Many legends draw a box with "GT"
Two-shaft turbines show a separate power turbine trapezoid

symbols.name: Gas turbine generator set
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 / IEC 60617 (G)
symbols.drawn: A gas turbine (two trapezoids with a combustor circle, or a box marked GT) on a shaft to a circle marked "G".
symbols.meaning: Main power generation: a gas turbine driving a generator, running on fuel gas with diesel backup. Becomes gas-turbine-generator.
variants: Electrical drawings show only the G circle on the single-line diagram

symbols.name: Gas-turbine-driven compressor train
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A gas turbine symbol on a shaft to a compressor trapezoid.
symbols.meaning: Gas-turbine-driven centrifugal compressor (export or injection). Becomes gas-turbine-compressor.
variants: Electric-motor-driven compressors show an M circle instead (then centrifugal-compressor)

symbols.name: Steam turbine
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 (group 20)
symbols.drawn: A trapezoid widening in the flow direction, with steam in at the narrow end and exhaust at the wide end, and a shaft to the driven machine.
symbols.meaning: Steam turbine driver: onshore and refinery pumps, compressors and generators. Not used offshore. No dedicated component.
variants: A turbine trapezoid widens in the flow direction; a compressor trapezoid narrows

symbols.name: Electric motor (driver)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 / IEC 60617
symbols.drawn: A circle containing "M" joined by a shaft line to the driven pump, fan or compressor.
symbols.meaning: Electric motor driver. Usually part of the pump or compressor package; becomes electric-motor if modelled separately.
variants: Variable-speed motors are marked VSD/VFD or have a diagonal arrow
Electrical drawings use "M" with "3~"

symbols.name: Diesel engine (driver)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 (group 20)
symbols.drawn: A rectangle marked "DE" (or "D"), joined by a shaft to the driven machine, with fuel and exhaust connections.
symbols.meaning: Diesel engine driver: firewater pumps, emergency and essential generators, crane engines. With a pump it is diesel-firewater-pump; with a generator it is diesel-generator.
variants: ISO draws an engine as a rectangle with a cross or a piston mark

symbols.name: Diesel generator set
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 16, 17 and 20, compressors, blowers, engines) / PIP PIC001 / IEC 60617 (G)
symbols.drawn: A "DE" rectangle on a shaft to a "G" circle.
symbols.meaning: Emergency or essential diesel generator: starts on main power failure and feeds the emergency switchboard. Becomes diesel-generator.
variants: On the single-line diagram only the G circle is shown

symbols.name: Filter (general)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001 (group 6)
symbols.drawn: A vessel outline divided by a dashed line (the filter medium), with inlet on one side and outlet on the other.
symbols.meaning: Any filter: liquid filter, gas filter, bag filter. If cartridges are drawn it is cartridge-filter; with a coalescing and vane section it is filter-separator.
variants: Some legends draw a rectangle with a dashed diagonal
Duplex filters are two such vessels with changeover valves

symbols.name: Cartridge filter
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A vertical vessel with a tubesheet line across it and several narrow rectangles (cartridges) hanging from it.
symbols.meaning: Cartridge filter or coalescer housing: fuel-gas filters, injection-water polishing, chemical filters. Becomes cartridge-filter.
variants: Bag filters are drawn with U-shaped bags
A dp gauge (PDI) is almost always drawn across it

symbols.name: Media filter (multimedia / nutshell)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A vertical vessel partly filled with a dotted area (the filter bed), with an inlet distributor on top and a collector at the bottom.
symbols.meaning: Deep-bed filter: seawater injection filtration, produced-water nutshell filters. Usually several in parallel with backwash. Becomes water-filter-package.
variants: Layers may be shown with different hatching (anthracite, sand, garnet)

symbols.name: Filter-separator / coalescer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A horizontal vessel with two sections: filter or coalescer elements (dashed rectangles) in the first, a vane pack (zig-zag) in the second, and a liquid sump under each.
symbols.meaning: Two-stage gas filter-separator: fuel-gas and seal-gas conditioning, sales-gas polishing. Becomes filter-separator.
variants: Vertical coalescers are drawn as a vertical vessel with cartridges
Liquid-liquid coalescers show a hatched coalescing pack

symbols.name: Cyclone (gas-solid or gas-liquid)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001 (group 8)
symbols.drawn: A cylinder on top of a cone pointing down, with a tangential inlet at the side of the cylinder, a gas outlet tube dipping in from the top and a solids or liquid outlet at the cone tip.
symbols.meaning: Centrifugal separator. In oil and gas, cyclonic internals and cyclone separators remove liquids or sand from gas. No dedicated component; desanders and hydrocyclones have their own.
variants: Multicyclone banks are drawn as several small cones in one vessel

symbols.name: Hydrocyclone (de-oiling liner)
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A long narrow cone lying on its side: tangential inlet at the wide end, a small reject (oil) outlet on the axis at the wide end, and the clean water outlet at the narrow tip. Packages show a vessel holding many liners.
symbols.meaning: De-oiling hydrocyclone for produced water: removes oil droplets by spinning. Becomes hydrocyclone-package (the vessel with liners and its reject and water lines).
variants: Package P&IDs draw one vessel with "liners" written inside
Desanding hydrocyclones are the same shape, mounted vertically, with sand out at the tip

symbols.name: Desander
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A vertical vessel with an inverted cone (cyclone liner) inside and a sand accumulator chamber at the bottom with a sand dump valve.
symbols.meaning: Wellhead or produced-water desander: removes sand before the separators. Becomes desander.
variants: Multiple liners in one vessel are drawn as several cones
The sand outlet goes to a sand-handling or jetting system (SD lines)

symbols.name: Agitator / mixer in vessel
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001 (group 28)
symbols.drawn: A vessel or tank with a motor (M) on top, a shaft running down into the liquid, and an impeller (two short blades or a propeller) at the bottom.
symbols.meaning: Stirred vessel: chemical make-up tanks, mud tanks, polymer and flocculant mixing. Model the tank; note the agitator.
variants: ISO shows different impeller marks (propeller, anchor, turbine)
Side-entry mixers come in through the shell

symbols.name: Static (in-line) mixer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A short in-line rectangle on the pipe with alternating diagonal or helical elements inside.
symbols.meaning: Motionless mixer: mixes injected chemicals, wash water or demulsifier into the main flow. No dedicated component.
variants: Mixing valves (globe-type) and mixing tees are drawn as valves and tees

symbols.name: Silencer
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (groups 6, 8 and 28, filters, separators, agitators) / PIP PIC001 / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A short fat cylinder (rounded rectangle) on a vent, exhaust or blow-off line, with baffles or a perforated tube inside.
symbols.meaning: Reduces noise: gas-turbine exhausts, PSV and blowdown discharges to atmosphere, steam vents. No dedicated component; vent-stack may include one.
variants: Often written simply as "SILENCER" on the line

symbols.name: Flare stack / tip
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / API 537
symbols.drawn: A tall vertical stack with a flame shape at the tip, often with a molecular seal (a bulge) below the tip and pilot and ignition lines.
symbols.meaning: Elevated flare: burns relief and blowdown gas. Becomes flare-stack (offshore booms are flare-boom).
variants: Ground or enclosed flares are drawn as a box with a flame
HP and LP tips may be drawn side by side

symbols.name: Flare boom
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / API 537
symbols.drawn: A long lattice boom (two parallel lines with a zig-zag between them) angled up and out from the platform edge, with the flare header inside it and a flame at the tip.
symbols.meaning: Offshore flare boom carrying the flare header out from the platform. Becomes flare-boom.
variants: P&IDs often draw it as a flare stack with "BOOM" noted

symbols.name: Flare knock-out drum
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / API 521
symbols.drawn: A horizontal drum with flare inlets at one or both ends on top, the gas outlet to the flare from the top centre, and a liquid outlet underneath (often to pumps).
symbols.meaning: Flare KO drum: catches liquid droplets before the flare. Becomes horizontal-separator with service KO, fed by the flare header.
variants: Vertical KO drums are drawn as a vertical vessel
Liquid seal drums (water seal) are drawn with a dip pipe

symbols.name: Cold vent stack
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / API 521
symbols.drawn: A vertical stack with an open top and no flame, sometimes with a small rain cap or dispersion arrows at the top.
symbols.meaning: Atmospheric vent for low-pressure hydrocarbon vents (TEG still, flash, riser blowdown). Becomes vent-stack.
variants: A flame arrester or snuffing connection may be drawn at the tip

symbols.name: Pig launcher
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: An enlarged barrel (a fat pipe section) with a quick-opening closure door (thick bar) at the back end, a reducer to the pipeline at the front, a kicker line from the back of the barrel through a valve to the main line, and a flow arrow away from the door.
symbols.meaning: Launches pigs into an export pipeline or flowline. Becomes pig-launcher. A pig signaller (XI) is often drawn on the outgoing line.
variants: The pig itself may be drawn as a dashed bullet inside the barrel
Pressure gauges, vents and drains on the barrel are typical

symbols.name: Pig receiver
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: The mirror of a launcher: the pipeline enters through a reducer into the enlarged barrel, which ends at a closure door, with a bypass line and a flow arrow towards the door.
symbols.meaning: Receives pigs at the end of a pipeline. Becomes pig-launcher (the same component serves launcher and receiver).
variants: A pig basket or bar tee at the barrel outlet may be drawn

symbols.name: Christmas tree (wellhead valves)
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 (API 6A)
symbols.drawn: A vertical stack of valves on the wellhead: lower and upper master valves, a cross with a production wing valve (actuated) and a kill wing to the side, a swab valve and tree cap on top, and a choke on the production wing outlet.
symbols.meaning: Surface christmas tree on a well. The upper master (SSV) and production wing valves are usually actuated and tripped by the wellhead control panel. Becomes christmas-tree; the wing outlet line goes to the manifold through the choke.
variants: Each valve may carry its tag (LMV, UMV/SSV, PWV, KWV, SV)
The SCSSV downhole is drawn as a valve in the tubing below the wellhead
Annulus valves (A/B annulus) appear on the wellhead below the tree

symbols.name: Production / test manifold
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: Two parallel headers (production and test) with several incoming well lines; each well line has a valve to each header, so one well at a time can be routed to test.
symbols.meaning: Gathers well flowlines into the production header and diverts one well to the test separator. Becomes production-manifold (slots = number of well inlets).
variants: Three-header manifolds add an HP/LP or a gas-lift header
Multi-port selector valves (MSV) replace the valve pairs on newer designs

symbols.name: BOP stack
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 (API 16A / 53)
symbols.drawn: A vertical stack: an annular preventer on top (a rounded block), then two or three ram blocks (rectangles with rams drawn as opposing filled triangles), with choke and kill side outlets and valves.
symbols.meaning: Blowout preventer stack on the wellhead during drilling and workover. Becomes bop-stack; the side outlets go to the choke & kill manifold (choke-manifold).
variants: Ram types are written beside each block (pipe, blind, shear)

symbols.name: Riser
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A line running from the topsides down through the sea surface (a wavy line) to the seabed (a hatched line), where it turns into the pipeline; often with an ESDV at the top and "RISER" or a pipeline number written on it.
symbols.meaning: Pipeline riser: import or export riser on the jacket. Becomes riser; the topsides riser ESDV is a separate esd-valve.
variants: Subsea isolation valves (SSIV) are drawn on the pipeline near the riser base
Flexible risers are drawn wavy

symbols.name: Package / skid (generic)
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A rectangle (often inside a dash-dot boundary) labelled with the package tag and name, standing on skid rails, with connections crossing its edge.
symbols.meaning: Vendor package whose internals are on the vendor P&IDs. Map it by name to the matching package component: chemical-injection-skid, instrument-air-package, teg-regeneration, nitrogen-generator, hydraulic-power-unit, hydrocyclone-package, water-filter-package, hypochlorite-generator or metering-skid.
variants: On overview P&IDs, packages are often a single labelled box

symbols.name: Chemical injection package
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001
symbols.drawn: A dash-dot package boundary holding a chemical tank (or tote) and one or more metering pumps (pump circles with diagonal arrows), with injection lines leaving to the process.
symbols.meaning: Chemical injection skid: corrosion and scale inhibitor, demulsifier, methanol, biocide, antifoam. Becomes chemical-injection-skid (outlets = number of injection lines).
variants: Methanol packages are drawn the same
Each injection line often has a flow indicator and a check valve at the injection quill

symbols.name: Fiscal metering skid
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / API MPMS / ISO 5167
symbols.drawn: A dash-dot boundary with an inlet header, two or more parallel meter runs (each with isolation valves and a meter box or FE), an outlet header, and often a prover connection and a sampler.
symbols.meaning: Fiscal (custody transfer) metering for oil or gas export. Becomes metering-skid; a compact prover (compact-prover) is usually connected.
variants: Gas skids use ultrasonic or orifice runs; oil skids use turbine, Coriolis or ultrasonic runs
Flow computers are drawn as hexagons (computer functions)

symbols.name: Meter prover (compact piston prover)
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / API MPMS ch. 4
symbols.drawn: A cylinder with a piston (a short vertical bar) inside and detector marks, with inlet and outlet connections and a 4-way or double-block valves to the meter runs.
symbols.meaning: Calibrates the fiscal meters in place. Becomes compact-prover.
variants: Pipe (ball) provers are drawn as a long U-loop with launching chambers

symbols.name: Hydraulic power unit (HPU)
symbols.standard: Company / operator legend practice (API 6A, API 521, API 537) / PIP PIC001 / ISO 1219-1
symbols.drawn: A dash-dot package with an oil reservoir (open-top tank), a pump with a motor, and an accumulator (a capsule split by a line), with hydraulic supply and return lines leaving.
symbols.meaning: Wellhead HPU supplying hydraulic pressure to the SSVs, SCSSVs and wing valves through the wellhead control panel. Becomes hydraulic-power-unit.
variants: Accumulators alone (ISO 1219) are a capsule with a horizontal dividing line

symbols.name: Gas cylinder bank
symbols.standard: ISO 10628-2 (C0002 gas cylinder)
symbols.drawn: A row of tall narrow cylinders with domed tops (gas bottles), each with a valve, joined to a common manifold.
symbols.meaning: Bottle rack or quad of compressed gas: nitrogen backup, calibration gas. Becomes gas-cylinder-quad. CO2 or inert-gas fire-suppression banks are drawn the same but belong to fire & gas.
variants: A single bottle is one cylinder symbol
Quads are often drawn as one box labelled "N2 QUAD"

symbols.name: Point gas detector (flammable)
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A small bubble (or hexagon or triangle, by legend) with "GD", often with the gas noted (HC, CH4) and the zone or voting group beside it.
symbols.meaning: Catalytic or infrared point detector for flammable gas, alarming at about 20 % LEL and confirming at about 60 % LEL with 2ooN voting. Becomes point-gas-detector.
variants: F&G layouts differ a lot: circles, triangles or hexagons with GD, IR, HC or "G"
P&IDs may draw it as an ISA bubble AT/AE with "LEL"
Duct (HVAC inlet) detectors are drawn on the duct

symbols.name: Toxic gas detector (H2S, CO)
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A detector bubble marked with the toxic gas, usually "H2S" (or "CO").
symbols.meaning: Electrochemical toxic gas detector, usually H2S with alarms at about 5 and 10 ppm. Becomes toxic-gas-detector. Hydrogen detectors (battery rooms) are marked "H2" and become hydrogen-detector.
variants: Some legends use a triangle with T or TOX

symbols.name: Open-path (line-of-sight) gas detector
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A transmitter box and a receiver box joined by a dashed beam line, marked OGD or Tx/Rx.
symbols.meaning: Infrared beam detector covering a path (LEL·m), for perimeters and modules. Becomes open-path-gas-detector.
variants: Some legends draw a single box with a long dashed arrow

symbols.name: Acoustic (ultrasonic) gas leak detector
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A detector bubble with "UGD" and curved sound arcs beside it.
symbols.meaning: Ultrasonic leak detector that hears high-pressure gas leaks, independent of wind dilution. Becomes acoustic-gas-leak-detector.
variants: Some legends mark it "AGLD" or draw a microphone symbol

symbols.name: Flame detector
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A detector bubble with "FD" and a dashed cone showing its field of view.
symbols.meaning: Optical flame detector (IR3, UV/IR), voting 2ooN for confirmed fire. Becomes flame-detector.
variants: ISA letter B (burner, combustion) is used on some P&IDs: BE or BS
The cone shows the aiming direction on F&G layouts

symbols.name: Heat detector
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A detector bubble with "HD" (sometimes a TSH bubble, or a square in building legends).
symbols.meaning: Fixed-temperature or rate-of-rise heat detector in enclosures, turbine hoods and accommodation. Becomes heat-detector.
variants: Building fire-alarm legends (NFPA 170, BS 5839) use their own forms; check the legend
Linear heat-detection cable is drawn as a dashed line with LHD

symbols.name: Smoke detector
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72
symbols.drawn: A detector bubble with "SD".
symbols.meaning: Point smoke detector (optical or ionisation) in control rooms, LERs, E-houses and quarters. Becomes smoke-detector. Beam detectors (beam-smoke-detector) and aspirating systems (aspirating-smoke-detector) are separate components.
variants: Aspirating (VESDA) systems are a box "ASD" with a sampling pipe with holes
Beam smoke detectors are drawn as a Tx/reflector pair
In-duct smoke detectors are drawn on the HVAC duct

symbols.name: Manual call point (MAC)
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72 / ISO 7240-11
symbols.drawn: A square with a smaller filled circle inside (the break-glass button), sometimes marked MAC or MCP.
symbols.meaning: Manual alarm call point. Pressing it raises a fire alarm (and on many platforms initiates ESD or GA). Becomes manual-call-point. ESD push-buttons look similar but are marked ESD.
variants: Yellow (ESD) vs red (fire) call points are only told apart by text or colour
NFPA-style legends: a small rectangle with "F" or "MS" (manual station)

symbols.name: Alarm beacon (visual)
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72 / IEC 60617 (signal lamp)
symbols.drawn: A circle with an X inside (the IEC lamp symbol) and short rays around it, often with the colour noted (red, yellow, blue).
symbols.meaning: Flashing beacon for general alarm, gas or fire alarm, CO2 release or prepare-to-abandon. Colour gives the meaning. Becomes alarm-beacon.
variants: Some legends draw a dome with rays or write "B" in a circle
Often combined with a sounder as one device

symbols.name: Alarm sounder / bell
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72 / IEC 60617 (bell, sounder)
symbols.drawn: A half-circle dome sitting on a flat base line (the IEC bell or sounder), with its connection below.
symbols.meaning: Electronic sounder or bell for fire, gas and general alarm. Usually paired with a beacon; becomes alarm-beacon (beacon and sounder). Large-area PA/GA horns are the loudspeaker symbol.
variants: Horn symbols (a trumpet shape) are also used for sounders

symbols.name: PA/GA loudspeaker (horn)
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72 / IEC 60617 (loudspeaker)
symbols.drawn: A small rectangle with a flared trumpet (trapezoid) opening out of it, the IEC loudspeaker or horn.
symbols.meaning: PA/GA horn loudspeaker carrying alarm tones and voice messages across the plant. Becomes pa-loudspeaker.
variants: Ceiling speakers in buildings are drawn as a circle with a small square

symbols.name: Deluge valve
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 15)
symbols.drawn: A valve drawn filled (normally closed) on the firewater supply with a trip actuator on top (often a solenoid "S" box or hydraulic latch), and "DV" or the deluge zone written beside it. Open (dry) pipework leads to the nozzles downstream.
symbols.meaning: Deluge valve: opens on confirmed fire (or manually) to flood a zone through open nozzles. Becomes deluge-valve-skid (valve set with isolations, trim and test line).
variants: Alarm check valves for wet sprinkler systems look similar and are marked "ACV"
The skid usually shows LO isolation valves either side

symbols.name: Sprinkler head (closed)
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 13)
symbols.drawn: A small drop from the pipe ending in a closed head: a small filled circle (the glass bulb) with a short deflector bar.
symbols.meaning: Automatic sprinkler: opens on its own when its bulb bursts. Used in quarters, workshops and stores. Becomes deluge-nozzle, which also covers sprinkler heads.
variants: Building legends draw a small circle with a cross, or a filled dot
Upright vs pendent is written beside it

symbols.name: Deluge (open) spray nozzle
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 15)
symbols.drawn: A small drop from the pipe ending in an open nozzle (a small triangle), with dashed spray lines fanning out.
symbols.meaning: Open water-spray nozzle on deluge pipework. All nozzles in the zone discharge together when the deluge valve opens. Becomes deluge-nozzle.
variants: Foam-water nozzles are drawn the same with "F"
Nozzle layouts are usually on separate fire-protection drawings

symbols.name: Water mist nozzle / system
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 750)
symbols.drawn: A nozzle on a small-bore line with a fine dotted spray cone, often inside an enclosure outline and marked "WM".
symbols.meaning: High-pressure water mist for turbine hoods, generator enclosures and machinery spaces. Usually a vendor package with its own pump and cylinders. No dedicated component.
variants: Mist skids are drawn as a package box with cylinders or a pump

symbols.name: Fire hydrant
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A pillar on the firewater main with a cap on top and two hose outlets on the sides.
symbols.meaning: Hydrant on the firewater ring main for hoses. Mostly onshore; offshore uses hose reels and monitors. Becomes fire-hydrant.
variants: Plot-plan legends draw a circle with a cross or a filled half-circle

symbols.name: Fire monitor
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A riser from the firewater main with a swivel joint (circle) on top and a nozzle barrel angled out of it, sometimes with an arc showing its sweep.
symbols.meaning: Fixed water or foam monitor covering helidecks, wellbays and tank areas. Becomes fire-monitor.
variants: Remote-controlled monitors carry an M actuator
Foam-water monitors are marked "F"

symbols.name: Fire hose reel
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A drum (two concentric circles) fed from the firewater line through a valve, with a hose ending in a nozzle.
symbols.meaning: Fire hose reel at escape routes and process areas. Becomes hose-reel.
variants: Foam hose reels are marked "F"
Layout legends draw a circle with "HR"

symbols.name: Portable fire extinguisher
symbols.standard: ISO 7010 (F001) / NFPA 170 / company layout practice
symbols.drawn: A canister outline with a handle and short hose, marked with the agent: DP (dry powder), CO2, F (foam) or W (water).
symbols.meaning: Portable or wheeled extinguisher. Shown on safety layouts more than P&IDs. Becomes fire-extinguisher.
variants: Layouts often use a triangle or circle with the agent letters
Wheeled units are drawn with wheels

symbols.name: Firewater pump (diesel driven)
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 20)
symbols.drawn: A pump (centrifugal circle, or a vertical turbine pump into a caisson) driven by a "DE" diesel engine box, discharging into the firewater ring main.
symbols.meaning: Diesel firewater pump that starts on low ring-main pressure or a fire signal. Becomes diesel-firewater-pump. Electric firewater and jockey pumps are drawn with M.
variants: Offshore pumps are usually vertical caisson pumps with a right-angle gearbox
Jockey pumps keep the ring main pressurised and are drawn small with M

symbols.name: Foam system (concentrate tank and proportioner)
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 11)
symbols.drawn: A small vertical tank of foam concentrate (marked AFFF or F) joined to an in-line proportioner (a venturi-like body) on the firewater line.
symbols.meaning: AFFF foam skid: proportions foam concentrate into firewater for helideck and wellbay monitors and deluge. No dedicated component.
variants: Bladder tanks are drawn with an internal bladder line
Some legends write "FOAM" in a box

symbols.name: CO2 / inert gas extinguishing system
symbols.standard: NFPA 15 / NFPA 13 / NFPA 20 / ISO 13702 (fire protection) / company legend practice (NFPA 12 / NFPA 2001)
symbols.drawn: A bank of cylinders on a manifold with a release valve, piped to discharge nozzles inside an enclosure outline, marked CO2, IG-541 or N2.
symbols.meaning: Total-flooding gas system for turbine hoods, switch rooms and generator enclosures. The release is interlocked with a beacon and sounder and the enclosure dampers. No dedicated component (gas-cylinder-quad is for nitrogen bottles).
variants: Clean-agent (FM-200, Novec) systems are drawn the same

symbols.name: Safety shower and eyewash
symbols.standard: ANSI Z358.1 / ISO 7010 (E012) / company legend practice
symbols.drawn: A shower head (an inverted cone) on a pipe stand, often with a small eyewash bowl on the side, fed from potable water.
symbols.meaning: Emergency shower and eyewash station near chemical injection, battery rooms and laboratories. Becomes safety-shower.
variants: Layout legends use the ISO 7010 E012 / E011 pictograms

symbols.name: Fusible plug loop
symbols.standard: Offshore F&G layout practice (ISA 5.1-style letter codes) / ISO 7240 / NFPA 72 / API RP 14C
symbols.drawn: An instrument-air (pneumatic //) loop with small fusible plug elements (small filled squares marked FP) placed around the wellhead or equipment.
symbols.meaning: Pneumatic fire detection: a plug melts in a fire, the loop pressure falls, and the wellhead or package shuts in. Classic on wellhead platforms. Not modelled; note it on the trees.
variants: API RP 14C tags them TSE
Some legends draw a circle with "FP" on the loop

symbols.name: Two-winding transformer
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: Two overlapping circles (one per winding) on the single-line diagram, with the rating and vector group written beside them.
symbols.meaning: Power or distribution transformer, e.g. 11/0.69 kV. Becomes transformer. ANSI drawings show two facing coils instead.
variants: A diagonal arrow through the circles = on-load tap changer
Winding symbols (Δ, Y, Yn) may be drawn inside the circles

symbols.name: Three-winding transformer
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: Three overlapping circles in a triangle: one primary on top, two secondaries below.
symbols.meaning: Transformer with two secondary windings, e.g. feeding two switchboard sections or a 12-pulse VFD. Becomes transformer.
variants: Autotransformers are a single circle with a tap

symbols.name: Circuit breaker
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A switch (a lead with a diagonal blade) with a small × on the fixed contact.
symbols.meaning: Circuit breaker that makes, carries and interrupts fault current: incomers, feeders and bus ties. Inside a switchboard it is part of switchgear. In an outdoor substation (air-insulated bay) it becomes hv-circuit-breaker.
variants: ANSI legends draw a square box or two arcs; draw-out breakers show chevrons (» «) above and below
A filled square is often used for a closed breaker on SLD overviews

symbols.name: Disconnector (isolator)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A switch blade with a short bar across the fixed contact.
symbols.meaning: Off-load isolator giving a visible break for maintenance. Inside a switchboard it is part of switchgear. In an outdoor substation it becomes disconnector.
variants: Switch-disconnectors (load-break) add a small circle on the contact as well

symbols.name: Earthing switch
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A disconnector blade whose lower side goes straight to an earth symbol, branching off a main circuit.
symbols.meaning: Earths a circuit or busbar for safe maintenance, interlocked with the breaker. Inside a switchboard it is part of switchgear. In an outdoor substation it is the earthing blade of a disconnector (disconnector).
variants: Often drawn beside a cable feeder below the breaker

symbols.name: Fuse
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A small rectangle with the conductor line passing straight through it.
symbols.meaning: Fuse protecting a circuit, VT or small motor feeder. Part of switchgear or distribution boards; not modelled.
variants: A fuse-switch combines a switch blade with the fuse rectangle

symbols.name: Contactor
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A switch blade with a small half-circle on the fixed contact.
symbols.meaning: Motor starter contactor in an MCC bucket: switches motors on and off, often with a thermal overload. Part of the MCC (switchgear); not modelled.
variants: Starters may be drawn as a box with "DOL", "Y/Δ" or "SS" (soft starter)

symbols.name: Motor (electrical)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A circle containing "M" and "3~" at the end of a feeder.
symbols.meaning: Three-phase induction motor load with its kW rating. On the SLD it is the motor of a pump, fan or compressor; becomes electric-motor if modelled separately.
variants: "M" with "1~" = single-phase
Synchronous motors are marked "MS"

symbols.name: Generator
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A circle containing "G" (often with a "~"), at the top of a feeder to the switchboard.
symbols.meaning: AC generator. On the SLD its driver is written beside it: GT means gas-turbine-generator, DG means diesel-generator.
variants: Some legends draw a circle with a sine wave only

symbols.name: Variable frequency drive (VFD)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A square split by a diagonal, with "~" in both halves (an AC/AC converter), feeding a motor.
symbols.meaning: Variable-speed drive for large pumps, compressors and fans. Becomes vfd-cabinet.
variants: Some legends draw two boxes: rectifier (~/=) then inverter (=/~)
Often written VSD

symbols.name: Uninterruptible power supply (UPS)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A rectifier box (~/=) and an inverter box (=/~) in series with a battery between them, often inside a dashed frame with a static bypass.
symbols.meaning: UPS that keeps control, F&G, ESD and telecom systems running on mains failure. Becomes ups-battery-cabinet.
variants: DC UPS systems show only the rectifier (charger) and the battery

symbols.name: Battery
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: Pairs of parallel plates: a long thin line (positive) and a short thick line (negative), repeated.
symbols.meaning: Battery bank for a UPS, a diesel engine start or switchgear tripping. Becomes ups-battery-cabinet when it is the UPS or DC battery room.
variants: A dashed line between two cells means many cells in series

symbols.name: Busbar
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A thick horizontal line with feeders dropping from it, labelled with the board name and voltage.
symbols.meaning: Switchboard busbar section: main, essential and emergency boards. The busbar belongs to the switchboard (switchgear); it is not modelled separately.
variants: Bus couplers (ties) are drawn as a breaker linking two bars
Double busbars are two parallel thick lines

symbols.name: Current transformer (CT)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A small circle around the conductor line, with secondary leads to a meter or relay.
symbols.meaning: Steps down current for protection relays and meters. Inside a switchboard it is part of switchgear. A free-standing outdoor CT becomes instrument-transformer.
variants: Ratio (e.g. 400/1 A) and class are written beside it
Some legends draw a small loop on the conductor

symbols.name: Voltage transformer (VT)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: Two small overlapping circles (like a power transformer, but smaller), on a fused tap from the busbar, with the secondary earthed.
symbols.meaning: Steps down voltage for metering, protection and synchronising. Inside a switchboard it is part of switchgear. A free-standing outdoor VT/CVT becomes instrument-transformer. Don't confuse it with a power transformer (bigger, in the main feeder path).
variants: ANSI legends call it a PT (potential transformer)

symbols.name: Surge arrester
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A rectangle with a downward arrow inside, connected between the conductor and earth.
symbols.meaning: Protects transformers and cables from switching and lightning surges. Becomes surge-arrester in an outdoor substation or at a transformer; inside switchgear it is not modelled separately.
variants: Older legends show a spark gap (two arrows tip to tip)

symbols.name: Earth (ground)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A vertical lead ending in three horizontal lines that get shorter downward.
symbols.meaning: Connection to earth: neutral earthing, equipment and instrument earthing. Not modelled.
variants: Protective earth may be drawn in a circle
Clean (instrument) earth is sometimes marked IE

symbols.name: Capacitor
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: Two short parallel plates with a lead on each side.
symbols.meaning: Power-factor correction capacitor bank or harmonic filter. Part of switchgear; not modelled.
variants: Capacitor banks are often a single capacitor symbol with the kvar rating

symbols.name: Neutral earthing resistor (NER)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A rectangle (resistor) between a transformer or generator neutral point and an earth symbol.
symbols.meaning: Limits earth-fault current on an MV system. Becomes neutral-earthing-resistor.
variants: ANSI resistors are drawn as a zig-zag

symbols.name: Switchboard / MCC
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram symbols)
symbols.drawn: A dashed frame around a busbar with an incoming breaker and outgoing feeders (breakers or contactors), labelled with the board tag and voltage.
symbols.meaning: HV/LV switchboard or motor control centre. Becomes switchgear (set the kind: MV, LV or MCC), usually inside an E-house (e-house).
variants: MCC buckets are drawn as contactor + overload + motor
Overview SLDs show each board as a single bar

symbols.name: Junction box
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 / instrument and electrical layout practice
symbols.drawn: A small square marked "JB" with cables entering it.
symbols.meaning: Field junction box (Ex e) where field cables meet multicore cables. Usually on loop and layout drawings, not P&IDs. Becomes junction-box.
variants: Instrument JBs and power JBs are told apart by the tag (IJB, EJB)

symbols.name: Local control station (LCS)
symbols.standard: IEC 60617 / ISA 5.1 (HS) / company practice
symbols.drawn: A small box beside a motor marked "LCS", with start/stop push-buttons (small circles) or HS bubbles, and a dashed signal line to the MCC.
symbols.meaning: Field push-button station for local start/stop and emergency stop of a motor. Becomes local-control-station.
variants: P&IDs often show it as an HS bubble joined to the motor by a dashed line

symbols.name: Protection relay (ANSI device number)
symbols.standard: IEEE C37.2 (device numbers) / IEC 60617
symbols.drawn: A small circle or box with an ANSI device number (e.g. 50/51 overcurrent, 87 differential, 27 undervoltage), joined to a CT or VT by a dashed line.
symbols.meaning: Protection function inside the switchgear relay. Not on the plot; not modelled.
variants: IEC drawings may use symbolic forms (I>, I>>) instead of numbers
